540975|2026-06.headline: Aster DM Quality Care Q1 FY27 proforma revenue rose 20% YoY to INR 2,597 Cr, with EBITDA up 30% to INR 576 Cr and margin at 22.2%.
540975|2026-06.overview: First earnings call after the Aster DM Healthcare and Quality Care merger, effective 1 July 2026, so combined figures are proforma. Growth was volume-led, with over 2 million patients (up 13% YoY) and blended occupancy up 510 bps to 64%. Mature units (73% of revenue) grew 19% with 30% EBITDA margin, while Emerging units grew 63%. Management reiterated a 24-25% margin target within two to three years and a 10-15% synergy target, and said synergy benefits have not yet started to flow.

financial_highlights.change: Aster net cash INR 511 Cr; Quality Care debt INR 1,673 Cr

segments.name: Mature units
segments.commentary: 73% of revenue, grew 19% YoY on higher ARPP IP, better payor mix and MVT; EBITDA +29%, margin about 30% (+230 bps).

segments.name: Focus units
segments.commentary: 15% of revenue, revenue +16% YoY; EBITDA +20%, margin +60 bps. Management says these are running in the teens on EBITDA and need work.

segments.name: Emerging units
segments.commentary: Revenue +63% YoY; EBITDA +240%, margin 12.4% (+640 bps). Kasaragod reached EBITDA breakeven in June 2026, about 9 months after opening.

segments.name: Medical Value Travel (MVT)
segments.commentary: Revenue +62% YoY on new geographies; contribution still low versus peers, with management targeting double-digit share over a couple of years.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin target of 24-25% in two to three years post-merger; management said FY29 was not the right framing and expects a good exit in 2027 with targets reached between FY28 and FY29.
Synergy target of 10-15% incremental EBITDA, calculated on FY24 proforma EBITDA (about INR 150-200 Cr). Management reaffirmed it and said synergy benefits should show from this financial year.
Organic framework of 5-6% volume growth and 7-8% ARPP growth, which management says supports the margin target.
No quarterly or annual margin guidance will be given.
MVT growth expected to stay above 50% YoY.
Bed capacity to rise by about 4,170 beds over 3-4 years to over 15,000 beds; 53% brownfield-led.
capex_capacity: Trivandrum (Aster Capital) hospital expected to be operational in H2 FY27, around January 2027.
Hyderabad hospital expected to be operational around April 2027; medical equipment ordering to begin in 1-2 months.
Sarjapur (Bengaluru) facility of more than 450 beds in two blocks; phase I (Block A) expected in H2 FY28.

Cancer centre in Raipur to be inaugurated mid-August 2026. Bhubaneswar is a major project; Kottayam bed additions in 2028, with Nagercoil, Banjara Hills, Nampally and Shifa bed additions also planned.
Aster Women & Children block (159 beds) commissioned in April 2026 at Aster Whitefield, Bengaluru.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: Aster patient throughput +16% and ARPP IP +10%; in Kerala, IP volumes +16% and OP volumes +19%.
Robotics volumes up about 80% YoY; joint replacements +39%; transplants +19%. Orthopaedics, Neurology and Oncology each grew over 24%.
Karnataka recovered from single-digit growth in FY26 to about 16% in Q1, with 5-6% volume growth; 18+ doctors added in Bengaluru in Q1.
Management attributed Karnataka and Maharashtra softness to neighbourhood competition, expected to be temporary.
Medcity (Kerala) crossed INR 100 Cr revenue in two months of Q1 (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: How is the merged entity structured across the four clusters and the three India CEOs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clusters are based on geographic and business continuity, with parts of Kerala and Maharashtra grouped together and Andhra, Telangana, Central and part of East grouped. Clinical specialties and maturity cuts are being run as a matrix alongside the country CEOs.

qa_highlights.question: Is 24-25% margin achievable in FY27 after the strong start?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO declined to guide quarterly or yearly margins and said the company is on track for 24-25% in two to three years post-merger.

qa_highlights.question: What low-hanging margin levers remain, and what synergies are realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna said merger synergies have not yet played out; cohesive working started only in July. The 10-15% incremental EBITDA target is unchanged, with significant results expected from this financial year and annualising next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 19-20% growth in Bengaluru sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said growth in the lower-to-mid teens, or double digits, is sustainable. He added that competition dips typically last one or two quarters and that a general surgery team that had left has rejoined.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Maharashtra and Karnataka growing slower than the company average?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed Kerala's recovery to volume-led growth after the Q4 FY25 decline. Karnataka's slower growth was tied to doctor attrition in FY26 and competition, and management said it is now recovering.

qa_highlights.question: What are the timelines for the greenfield projects in Trivandrum, Hyderabad and Sarjapur?
qa_highlights.answer: Trivandrum is expected around January 2027 (H2 FY27), Hyderabad around April 2027, and Sarjapur phase I in H2 FY28.

risks_watch: Synergy delivery: 10-15% incremental EBITDA (INR 150-200 Cr) is still to be proven; management said results start in FY27.
Competitive intensity in Bengaluru and other micro-markets, which hit Karnataka growth earlier.
Merger execution: new leadership structure (three India CEOs, four maturity cuts) is still being finalised; reporting will change, with geographic data to follow in about a quarter.
Focus units (15% of revenue) are in the teens on EBITDA and need to reach mature levels.
Net debt of INR 1,162 Cr combined, with Quality Care carrying INR 1,673 Cr debt, and the INR 114 Cr exceptional cost.
Greenfield timelines (Trivandrum, Hyderabad, Sarjapur) and the Kasaragod ramp are key next-quarter milestones.

541083|2026-03.headline: Inflame guides FY27 chimney volumes to ~4 lakh (+45-50%) and Q4 FY26 demand was soft, with management reporting June-to-date recovery.
541083|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 revenue grew about 41-42% and EBITDA about 55%, with EPS up about 85%, but Q4 was weak as market demand softened and raw material costs rose to about 75% of revenue in H2 from about 70% in H1. Q4 revenue was about INR35-37 crore against an internal expectation of INR55-60 crore. Management said demand has recovered in the first two months of FY27, with monthly growth of 40-50%, and that it is tracking its 50% growth target. Price pass-through is not complete and is expected to finish in about 1.5-2 months, with efficiency and AI-based inspection offsets. The company also disclosed a 34% stake in a new BLDC motor and electronics associate, Tricoree Machmatrix, though no investment figures were given.

financial_highlights.change: up about 4-5 percentage points; main increase in Q4

segments.name: Chimneys
segments.commentary: Core product; Panchkula grew about 42% and Hyderabad about 31% in volume. Management expects chimneys to remain about 60-65% of revenue going forward.

segments.name: Built-in / new products (ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators, microwaves, dishwashers, hobs)
segments.commentary: Other products were about 5-10% of revenue in the past one to two years. Management said 25 new models were showcased in April; built-in ovens are being ramped, with dishwashers and microwaves targeted by December-January. Hobs BIS is expected to be finalised in September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: about 4 lakh chimneys (about 50% growth on 270,000) and about 45-50% growth in chimney volume and total revenue.
Revenue target of INR400 crore-plus in FY28, and INR500 crore in FY28-FY29, per management.
Gross margin expected to recover as price pass-through completes in about 1.5-2 months; management said it will absorb pressure through efficiency gains and expects some margin pressure in H1 FY27.
BLDC share of chimney production expected to rise to about 80% by end of FY27 from about 60% currently.
Management expects inventory of 40-50% to fall once motors and PCBs are made in India, timeline about 1-2 years.
capex_capacity: Panchkula CapEx of about INR10 crore for 50,000 sq ft of new construction; ground floor operational within days, adding about 12,000-15,000 chimneys of capacity; second part by 15 August and third by 30 September.
Hyderabad plant utilisation is not being prioritised; it is being used for premium and value-added products (built-in ovens, wine coolers, refrigerators, microwaves, dishwashers).
Tricoree Machmatrix Private Limited: associate with 34% Inflame stake, to manufacture BLDC motors first (about 1-1.5 years) then electronics (another 1-1.5 years); no investment amount disclosed.
Flamecraft (Hyderabad): Inflame holds 51% of sheet metal business; company is outsourcing sheet metal and other processes via joint ventures.
Management plans glass plant with zero manpower, to be considered once investment crosses INR250-300 crore; not yet committed.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 demand was soft; management attributed it to the Gulf/geopolitical situation and said major buyers (IFB, Crompton, Hindware, Havells) were short of orders.
Management said demand has recovered in April-May 2026, with monthly volumes above prior-year levels for two months; price negotiations are ongoing with some customers.
Price pass-through not 100%; management cited rupee depreciation, Middle East disruption, RMB appreciation and gas supply issues (about three weeks) as cost drivers.
Management claims complaint rate below 1.5% versus higher rates for Chinese suppliers; cites 10-year warranty products.
Approval cycle for new products: about 15 days to 1 month for KAFF; about 2-2.5 months for Hindware, Havells, IFB, Crompton.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 FY26 below the expected 30,000-32,000 chimneys per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to industry demand softness and geopolitical fears; major buyers were short of orders in Q4. No loss of orders was cited.

qa_highlights.question: Are you on track for 4 lakh chimneys in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said 270,000 in FY26 plus 50% growth implies about 4 lakh, and said the order position covers the planned growth for 2-3 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue growth only about 11% on about 20% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material share rose to about 75%, plus INR depreciation and gas supply issues; volume weakness was from market demand.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold on 50% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may be slightly lower but absolute profit should rise; AI-based inspection is expected to cut inspection time by 10-20% in 1-1.5 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company still on SME rather than main board?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not meet two criteria: paid-up capital of at least INR10 crore and net worth of at least INR75 crore. Will migrate once eligible.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high and what about exports?
qa_highlights.answer: High inventory reflects SKD/CKD imports for refrigerators, ovens and hobs; expected to fall with local manufacturing. Exports are being explored, but India OEM demand of about 6 lakh chimneys is the priority.

risks_watch: Dependence on China for BLDC motors, PCBs, switches and heating elements; BLDC motors reportedly 37-38% sourced from China, and possible BIS on motors.

541096|2026-03.headline: Bharat Parenterals FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose to INR 15.8 crores from INR 2.7 crores, driven by Innoxel's loss narrowing; standalone revenue fell 23% to INR 234 crores.
541096|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was broadly flat at INR 345.4 crores versus INR 340 crores, but the mix shifted: standalone BPL revenue fell about 23% to INR 234 crores on deferred export tenders, exits from low-margin volume and about two months of production downtime for upgrades. Innoxel's revenue rose 174% to INR 72.4 crores, its EBITDA loss narrowed by INR 23.5 crores, and it turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY26 (INR 1.4 crores). Varenyam Healthcare grew 13.7% to INR 58.4 crores and turned profitable. FY27 guidance is given by business: standalone 10-15% growth, Innoxel 35-45% growth, and Varenyam 20-25% growth, with management conceding the standalone base will only partially recover this year.

segments.name: BPL standalone (exports, injectables)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 234 crores (down about 23%), EBITDA INR 21 crores at 9% margin; capacity utilisation 48% general, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins; order book INR 171 crores.

segments.name: Innoxel Lifesciences (complex generics/CDMO, US/EU)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 72.4 crores (up 174%), EBITDA loss INR 6.9 crores; US FDA establishment inspection report received and EUGMP clearance from FAMHP with zero critical and zero major observations; 19 active partners and 42 assets in pipeline.

segments.name: Varenyam Healthcare (domestic branded)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 58.4 crores (up 13.7%), EBITDA INR 2.5 crores and PAT INR 2.3 crores; 45 active brands, top five brands INR 28.7 crores (about half of revenue); Sugammadex over INR 10 crores; PCPM up 31% YoY to over INR 3.85 lakh.

segments.name: Varenyam Biolifesciences (pre-revenue)
segments.commentary: Facility under construction with approved budget about INR 160 crores and CWIP about INR 33 crores (around 20% complete); commissioning targeted September 2027, first EUGMP filing Q1 FY29, first commercial supply Q4 FY29.

guidance_outlook: Standalone BPL: revenue growth 10-15% and EBITDA margin 10-15% in FY27; management expects only partial recovery this year, with full recovery to FY25 levels targeted in FY28.

Innoxel: revenue growth 35-45% and EBITDA margin 20-25% in FY27; first commercial CMO supply from Q2 FY27, two to three CMO products commercialising in the year, 10 new filings, 20 new partner deals targeted, out-licensing income INR 70-90 crores, first MHRA and Health Canada filings.
Varenyam Healthcare: revenue growth 20-25% and EBITDA margin 8-13% in FY27; field force to exceed 250, seven product launches including Remishot, and launch of a gynecology division.
Varenyam Biolifesciences: commissioning of manufacturing lines by September 2027 and validation by March 2028; remains pre-revenue through FY27.
Standalone peak revenue of INR 400-500 crores expected on a 2030 horizon, sequential over 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: BPL standalone utilisation is low (48% general, 21% beta-lactam, 24% cephalosporins); management says 10-15% growth is possible without fresh capex.
Upgrades to the general injectable vial line, beta-lactam water system and structural changes for EUGMP ran through FY26, costing about two months of production across all three blocks.
PIC/S and EUGMP inspections at standalone facilities are scheduled during FY27 and are expected to cause some disruption before certification.
Innoxel's facility is validated and cleared for commercial supply to the US and selected European markets; new capacity depreciation is weighing on PAT.
Varenyam Biolifesciences: CWIP about INR 33 crores against budget of about INR 160 crores; civil works 50% complete, equipment procurement about 40%.
demand_pricing: BPL order book of INR 171 crores gives FY27 visibility; growth is expected from Southeast Asia, Africa and MENA.

A $27 million tender order (Jan 2025 announcement) was delayed; orders were received in early March 2026, supply has started, and about 90% is expected to be covered in FY27 with small spillover into early FY28.
BPL filings: 214 dossiers submitted, 40 new product registrations across Africa, LATAM and Southeast Asia, over 350 live filings in more than 40 countries; Vietnam representative office opened.
Varenyam corporate hospital coverage is over 7,500 institutions across 26 states; 50 new corporate hospital tie-ups added in FY26; medical sales force grew from 190 to 211.

Innoxel: two 505(b)(2) assets (exhibit batches done, on stability) targeted for US filing in Q3 and Q4 FY27 under partner names; one asset is filed or partly filed in Europe, with filing planned later this month.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 standalone guidance of 10-15% growth on a base of about INR 230-250 crores rather than INR 300 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the base is FY26 revenue. It expects partial recovery in FY27, with disruption from PIC/S and EUGMP preparation and inspections, and full recovery to FY25 levels in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is standalone peak revenue INR 400-500 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 400-500 crores is the target for the standalone business, but sequentially over 3-4 years, with peak revenue framed from a 2030 standpoint.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Varenyam Bio's commercialisation timeline moved from 2027 to Q4 FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is running at least one quarter behind schedule, citing geopolitical disruption. Filing now starts around Q1 FY28, first EUGMP filing is Q1 FY29, and commercial supply is Q4 FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY27 guidances cut across segments, especially Varenyam?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said earlier guidance was not met, so the new ranges are softer and deliberately achievable. Varenyam's earlier INR 75-80 crore revenue ambition was not restated; FY27 growth is 20-25% with heavy investment in field force and a new division.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Innoxel's FY27 margin expansion, and how much is CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from milestone payments and fixed cost leverage. Commercial supply is limited to two or at most three products. Management would not quantify CDMO revenue share, saying own-product manufacturing revenue starts in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing of the two Innoxel 505(b)(2) assets and the CMO commercialisations?
qa_highlights.answer: The two 505(b)(2) assets are targeted for US filing in Q3 and Q4 FY27, filed in partner names. One CMO product commercialises in Q2 FY27 and a second between Q3 and Q4 FY27; Innoxel earns fees and milestones rather than profit share on CMO deals.

541096|2026-09.headline: Bharat Parenterals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 110% YoY to INR136.3 crores and the group swung to a INR11.8 crore profit after tax.
541096|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR136.3 crores (up 110% YoY, up 45% QoQ) with EBITDA of INR26.6 crores at a 17.3% margin, versus INR8.5 crores at 9.1% in Q1. Innoxel Life Sciences drove the improvement, with revenue of INR44.5 crores at a 33% EBITDA margin, while standalone revenue of INR78.6 crores was held back by a sharp input-cost-driven gross margin fall to 35%. Management maintained FY27 guidance for standalone and Varenyam Healthcare, and kept Innoxel's margin guidance under review until Q3. A preferential issue of about INR139 crores was approved, with the proceeds not yet in the 30 September balance sheet.

segments.name: Standalone (BPL)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR78.6 crores, with EBITDA INR7 crores at 9% margin, down from 12.3% in Q1, as input material costs rose about 5 percentage points of revenue. Domestic tender book fell from INR119 crores (June) to INR65 crores (September); total order book INR117 crores. Q2 included about INR25-30 crores of deferred export tender supply.

segments.name: Innoxel Life Sciences (55.9% owned)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR44.5 crores at 33% EBITDA margin, mostly licensing, milestone and development income. First CMO product (oral liquid) exported to the US on 20 October, after quarter end, with no revenue yet in Q2. Management maintains FY27 guidance of 35-40% revenue growth and 20-25% margin, excluding licensing income of INR80-90 crores.

segments.name: Varenyam Healthcare (domestic branded)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR19.7 crores (up 33.2% YoY), EBITDA margin 9.2%. H1 revenue INR44.9 crores (up 43.2%) at 11% margin. FY27 guidance is 20-25% growth and 8-13% margin; 229 field representatives against a year-end target of 250. Bhuvah women's health division launches later this year as a cost before revenue.

segments.name: Varenyam Biolifesciences (VBPL)
segments.commentary: Pre-revenue; Q2 operating cost INR0.14 crores and capital work in progress INR33.7 crores. Construction completion targeted for Q2 CY2028. Pivoted towards biologics CDMO with a 2,000 kL tank in phase 1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance maintained. Standalone: revenue growth 10-15% on FY26 base of INR234 crores; EBITDA margin 10-15%.

Innoxel: revenue growth 35-45% and EBITDA margin 20-25%, excluding licensing income of INR80-90 crores. H1 is well ahead on revenue but just under the band on margin; revisions, if any, to be given after Q3.
Innoxel targets 10-12 signed out-licensing contracts by end-Q3 FY27 (six signed in H1), against a target of 12-15 a year.
Varenyam Healthcare: 20-25% growth and 8-13% margin retained; business tapers into Q4 and the new division is a cost.
No further equity dilution expected; capex to be funded internally plus bank debt at Varenyam Biolifesciences. Up to INR135 crores of the preferential issue goes to subsidiaries over two years.
EU GMP inspection expected in FY27, with no confirmed date from the regulator.
capex_capacity: Standalone general block utilisation 70% in H1 FY27 vs 48.5% in FY26; beta-lactam 33% (vs 21%); cephalosporins 31.5% (vs 24%). Management says no new capacity is needed for standalone guidance.
Standalone H1 capex about INR15 crores against INR65 crores cash from operations.
Liposomal skid in the general block: exhibit batches planned for November; filing targeted for Q1 of next financial year.
Innoxel holds a US FDA EIR and a Belgian GMP certificate covering all four lines.
VBPL: Phase 1 capex about INR300 crores, with one 2,000 kL tank; construction completion targeted for Q2 CY2028 subject to commissioning and regulatory timelines; phase 2 scope not yet defined.
demand_pricing: Standalone order book INR117 crores at end-September across domestic tenders, exports and international tenders. Management says the book was priced before input cost increases, so margins will stay under pressure until prices ease or the book turns over.

Management is shifting standalone growth towards branded business via new registrations, dossier filings and EU GMP/PIC/S approvals; tender business is being fulfilled but not expanded. Tender share was about 52% of revenue per an analyst citation; management did not confirm the split.
Innoxel: 48 projects across 18-19 clients under CDMO and CMO banners. Upfront payments are 10% or less of Innoxel revenue; the rest is milestone-based.
Innoxel 505(b)(2) products expected to achieve 10-15% market conversion in the first couple of years, per partner views; management cited 70-80% gross margins typical for these contracts.
Innoxel profit-share economics for own CDMO products expected from Q3 FY28 (505(b)(2)); management said margins could exceed 35-40% once profit-share income starts, with no firm number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of standalone Q2 revenue came from the deferred export tender?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR25-30 crores in Q2, with part of the total also recognised in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Given H1 Innoxel revenue of about INR65 crores, why keep FY27 guidance of 35-40% growth on a INR72 crore base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said licensing and milestone income is lumpy; it will review Innoxel guidance after Q3 and currently expects to meet the guided numbers, keeping the 20-25% margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR139 crore preferential issue fund Varenyam Biolifesciences or Innoxel?
qa_highlights.answer: It is earmarked for all subsidiaries as requirements arise; no split was given. A monitoring agency has been appointed.

qa_highlights.question: Could Innoxel cross INR300 crores of revenue in FY29, and what margin profile applies at scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to commit to INR300 crores and will update in FY28. Margins should rise once profit share from own products starts, possibly above 35-40%, but no firm number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will further dilution be needed to fund VBPL and Innoxel?
qa_highlights.answer: No further dilution is expected; capex will be funded from Innoxel and standalone cash flow plus the INR139 crore raise, with bank debt at VBPL.

qa_highlights.question: Can Innoxel's complex products be launched in India through Varenyam?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate plans; Indian pricing does not support the product costs from Innoxel.

541153|2026-03.headline: Bandhan Bank Q4FY26 PAT rose 68% YoY to INR 534 crore, with NIM up to 6.2% and credit cost easing to 2%.
541153|2026-03.overview: Bandhan Bank reported Q4FY26 PAT of INR 534 crore, up 68% YoY and 159% QoQ, with ROA of 1.1% and ROE of 9% for the quarter. NIM rose to 6.2% from 5.9% in Q3 on a 23 bps QoQ fall in deposit costs, while credit cost fell to 2% from 3.3%. Slippages declined to INR 1,028 crore from INR 1,314 crore, led by EEB, and collection efficiency improved. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 1,224 crore, with NII down 5.8% YoY, and opex was elevated in Q4 by PSLC and IT items.

financial_highlights.change: from 31% last year; bulk deposits -7% YoY

segments.name: EEB (microfinance and related)

segments.name: Non-EEB book
segments.commentary: Non-EEB advances grew 25% YoY and form about two-thirds of total advances. Retail grew 46% YoY (CV, CE, auto, gold loans); wholesale grew 33% YoY.

segments.name: Secured book
segments.commentary: Secured book grew 25% YoY and forms about 56% of advances, against a target of 58% by March 2027.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Other income grew 10% YoY and 12% QoQ; third-party distribution income rose 34% YoY and processing fees rebounded.

guidance_outlook: ROA guided at 1.6%-1.7% (management also cited 1.6%-1.8%, give or take 10 bps) by exit FY27 (Q4FY27); management says it will work towards this, calling it a challenge.
NIM guided at around 6% on total assets (about 6.5% on earning assets) by exit FY27; a further 10-20 bps improvement expected over the next 2-3 quarters from term deposit repricing.
Credit cost guided at 1.6%-1.7% by Q4FY27 from 2% in Q4FY26; FY26 credit cost was 3%.
Advances growth targeted at around 14%-15%; deposit growth to be better than advances, but industry credit growth now exceeds deposit growth.
PSL certificate cost expected to fall about 50% in FY27 versus FY26 and to be nearly neutralised in FY28.
Opex-to-average-assets remains a focus; FY26 was about 4% against guidance. Other income to add about 10 bps to ROA.

Expected ECL transition impact about INR 1,250 crore (based on December 2025 portfolio), spread over 5 years at about INR 250 crore a year, or roughly 16-17 bps CRAR impact each year; flow impact still being computed under the latest circular.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 1,955 branches; housing finance centres largely upgraded to full banking branches, some merged with existing branches.
4,400 EEB banking units across the country.
Average LCR in Q4 ranged 130%-140%; period-end LCR about 131%, down from about 200% a year earlier as bulk deposits fell.
Capital adequacy 18.0% CRAR and 17.3% Tier 1; management says ample headroom for growth.
demand_pricing: Collection efficiency ex-NPA improved to 98.9% in March 2026 from 98.1% in December 2025; EEB quarter-wide efficiency 99.3% vs 98.2% in Q3.

Collection efficiency ex-bucket 99.6% for Q4 (99.3% in Q3) and 99.7% for March; management says no adverse effect on collections from elections or the Middle East war so far in April, though a few basis points dipped.
Deposit competition is intense; competitor deposit rates rose sharply in March 2026, and bank chose not to grow bulk deposits in Q4.
Yield on advances rose 14 bps QoQ, helped by the Q3 ARC sale removing NPAs from the base and the EEB mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII grow only 4% QoQ despite strong advance growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the back-ended loan growth (about 50% of incremental FY growth came in Q4, with late-March disbursals not yet earning), two fewer days in the quarter, and the 25 bps December repo cut impacting about 46% of the book (11 bps effect).

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state credit cost after the RBI ECL norms, and what are the standard asset provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds about INR 1,072 crore of standard asset provisions, including an extra 75 bps on standard assets: EEB at 1% vs 0.25% required, and personal loans/ABG at about 0.4%. Flow impact is still being computed; the INR 1,250 crore transition estimate is based on the December 2025 book.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins keep improving, and what is the NIM trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects another 10-20 bps of NIM improvement over the next 2-3 quarters as term deposits reprice, with a best-effort aim of about 6% NIM on total assets by exit FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the PSL shortfall and how will it be fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 PSLC cost was about INR 150 crore (INR 60 crore higher QoQ). The aim is a roughly 50% cut in FY27 and near zero in FY28, with EEB loans qualifying for PSL rising from about 10-15% to about 40%, targeting 60-65%.

qa_highlights.question: What were the one-off items in opex?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 120 crore in recurring-type items: PSLC cost up around INR 60 crore QoQ and IT expenses up around INR 50 crore, with timing-related elements expected not to repeat immediately. Separately, INR 73 crore extra employee cost came from keeping branches open on holidays.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a government deposit share and how much is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Government deposits are about INR 6,000 crore; about 12% of CASA is from government deposits. Retail composition, including CASA and retail term deposits, rose to 74% from 69% a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROA path and what would drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA rose from 0.2% in September to 0.4% in December and 1.1% in Q4. Drivers cited are lower credit cost, higher NIM, higher other income (about 10 bps expected), and lower PSLC costs; management acknowledged a 50-60 bps journey to the target.

risks_watch: Middle East war and fuel price or availability effects on the economy and collections; management has not quantified the impact.
ECL transition: about INR 1,250 crore (based on December 2025 data), with flow impact still to be computed under the latest RBI circular; the choice between P&L and reserves is pending.
Deposit cost pressure from intense competition; more term deposit renewals are due over the next 2-3 quarters.
Credit growth (about 14%-15% target) is running ahead of deposit growth across the industry; the bank has not added bulk deposits.
Non-recurring PSLC and IT costs; opex-to-assets was 4.4% in Q4 against about 4% for FY26.
Vishal Wadhwa (EEB head) resigned, citing personal career advancement; management says the process is now process-driven.
Management stated no NPA sale is currently planned, but an ARC-sale option remains open.
Media reports of promoter-level activity; management called them rumours and said there is no impact on the Bank's shareholding.

541167|2026-03.headline: Yasho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR246.7 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.1%; FY27 utilisation target is 75%+.
541167|2026-03.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR830 crore (up 22.7% YoY) with EBITDA of INR144 crore and margin of 17.4%, while Q4 revenue was INR246.72 crore (up 33%) with EBITDA of INR44.71 crore at 18.1%. Growth was entirely volume-led (FY26 volume up 33%), with management saying prices were under pressure until late March when 10-15% price increases started, mostly effective from April. Management guided to FY27 utilisation above 75% (from about 60% in FY26), volume growth of 35-45%, and a FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore tied to a 15-year long-term contract with INR51.4 crore advance. Leverage fell to 3.75x debt-to-EBITDA from 4.70x, and INR23.3 crore of FY27 liabilities were prepaid.

segments.commentary: Contributed 87% of revenue in both Q4 and full FY26 and is the key growth driver; management says all volume growth came from the industrial segment, with a slight dip on the consumer side.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Accounted for 62% of FY26 revenue; Americas demand improved in Q4 as tariffs moderated, and Europe is seeing some slowdown. Management is also starting to enter Asia.

FY27 volume growth of 35-45% (clarified after several restatements); EBITDA margin expected at least 2-3 percentage points above FY26, with a stated aim of about 20%.

Pricing pressure and margin pressure through FY26, with product mix shifted away from low-margin products.

Chinese competitors described as very strong and aggressive in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
India-EU FTA expected around early January; Yasho has a European team about one year old.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,500 crore FY28 target visible and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation rising to 85-90% by FY28, the special project coming on stream in FY28, and new rubber and lube molecules; the visibility is partly customer commitments made on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving into CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Yasho is not a CDMO and will not serve small-volume API-type orders of 20-100 metric tons. It will work with large-volume customers, with Pakhajan designed for 500-1,000 metric tons minimum per molecule.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Days have fallen from 215-216 in FY25 to about 190; the target is 170-175 over 6-12 months. Debtors are flat, and stock was useful in the supply crisis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 volume growth is from price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management measures growth in volume terms, and says price increases only started in late March and April 2026. Currency gains are largely offset by imported raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: Does Yasho make its own formulations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Yasho only makes pure chemicals and does not compete with its formulating customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MNC project capex included in the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR125 crore FY27 capex is separate; the share of capex attributable to the MNC project is zero.

risks_watch: Supply chain disruption from the Middle East: import delays, raw material shortages, and high petrochemical prices; management says high inventory has offset this so far.
Chinese competition in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
Europe slowdown and the timing of the India-EU FTA (expected around early January).
Working capital reduction to 170-175 days depends on raw material availability.

Ability to hold EBITDA margin as the customer price increases pass through, given management says costs cannot be fully passed on.

541167|2026-06.headline: Yasho Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 308 crore (volume +42% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 24.2%; management guides to sustain margins.
541167|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached a record Rs 308 crore, driven by 42% YoY volume growth from customer approvals and additional offtake in industrial chemicals. EBITDA rose to Rs 74.42 crore (24.2% margin, vs 17% previously cited), with PAT of Rs 36 crore (11.7% margin). Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.86x from 3.75x at Q4 FY26, bank loan ratings were upgraded to A- by CRISIL and ICRA, and working capital cycle shortened from 190 to 143 days. Management raised FY27 capex from Rs 125 crore to Rs 250 crore for two new buildings at Pakhajan and set a FY28 revenue target above Rs 1,600 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Highest quarterly revenue; 60% YoY growth per analyst question (not disputed)
From 3.75x at end of Q4 FY26

segments.name: Industrial chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 89% of Q1 revenue; management expects this to rise to about 90% going forward. Management said new-product revenue is about 30% of sales over the last two years, with revenue rising from Rs 600 crore to Rs 850 crore.

segments.name: Exports / geographies
segments.commentary: Export is about 69% of revenue; US sales recovered after tariff issues eased, and Europe and Middle East are growing. Asia and Africa are early-stage, with margins described as at par or slightly lower than US/Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained, given the Q1 benefit from the April price revision and operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gains to product mix and higher utilisation rather than stock gains, citing commitments from marquee customers to maintain margins.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to move EBITDA margin from the historical 17-20% range to about 24%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher utilisation (about 50% to 65%), higher customer offtake, product mix, and R&D-led process optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing and revenue potential of the Pakhajan capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 about Rs 100 crore and Phase 2 about Rs 150 crore, at about 2.5x asset turn. Management said the Rs 1,600 crore FY28 guidance excludes these buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain or raw material risks given the current macro environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is a genuine raw material supply issue, and export container bookings can take three to four weeks. Inventory fell, which drove working capital down.

qa_highlights.question: Margin differential between new and old products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products earn about 10-12% higher margin than older products. Newly launched products in the last 12 months carry better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Lube-additive and ICE exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not see EV adoption as a threat within a 10-year horizon, and that Rs 250 crore capex is not for lube alone.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to sustain the current EBITDA margin (about 24%) in FY27, though it said it cannot promise this beyond the next two to three years.
FY28 revenue target revised to more than Rs 1,600 crore; management said real growth from the new capacity comes from FY29.
Targets 30% to 40% annual revenue growth over the next few years.

Long-term agreement commercialisation expected in Q1 FY28, on track.

Vapi plant shut; efforts moved to Pakhajan, which also has a pilot facility for R&D.

Company is seeing more export traction than domestic; domestic sales are growing slowly.
Management cites a Rs 12-15 billion addressable market and an aspiration of $200-300 million revenue.

Delivery times reportedly unchanged at 8-10 weeks higher than before (per analyst question).

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin compress in Q1 and will it normalise?

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin return to 20-21% from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD S.V.S. Narayana Murty said yes, and that the Q1 shortfall was due to the raw-material and LPG issues.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 1,000 crore capex yielding EBITDA, and what is FY27 capex?

Scrap inventory policy and sales of titanium scrap; management says scrap is a strategic asset rather than surplus.

541233|2026-03.headline: FY26 was Lemon Tree's best year: revenue Rs 1,452.7 crore (+13%), PAT Rs 288.3 crore (+19%), with margin down 126 bps to 48.1%.
541233|2026-03.overview: Lemon Tree reported record FY26 and Q4 FY26 on occupancy, ARR, revenue, EBITDA, PBT, PAT and cash profit, with Q4 revenue of Rs 419.5 crore (+11%) and PAT of Rs 116.5 crore (+8%). Net EBITDA margin fell to 48.1% for FY26 and 52% for Q4, which management attributes to renovation spend, technology investment and the GST change. Management guided that these three cost heads fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28, and set out a proposed demerger that would leave Lemon Tree as an asset-light entity and Fleur Hotels as an owner/lessor platform. Q4 demand softened in March and April from the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, with corporate travel weaker and occupancy hitting what management called a ceiling.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever for a full financial year
from Rs 1,699 crore a year ago

segments.name: Lemon Tree (asset-light, managed and franchised)
segments.commentary: Opened 20 managed/franchised hotels (1,523 rooms) and signed 55 (4,912 rooms) in FY26; total pipeline 22,581 rooms across 268 hotels, of which 131 hotels and 11,811 rooms are operational. Keys RevPAR grew 20% and Aurika 19% for FY25 to FY26 on management's figures.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (owned/leased)
segments.commentary: Post-scheme, Fleur to have 5,600 rooms across 39 operational hotels; 4 hotels with 875 rooms in confirmed pipeline, including 572 rooms at Nehru Place (estimated capex Rs 700 crore). Fees Rs 95.8 crore, +8% on a same-store basis.

segments.name: Aurika brand
segments.commentary: Highest ARR and margin product; Aurika occupancy rose from 62% to 74% for FY26 with RevPAR +19%, though Q4 occupancy fell 2% as a large Mumbai wet-lease ended. Aurika has only two hotels (Mumbai and Udaipur).

guidance_outlook: Cost heads (GST impact, technology, renovation) expected to fall from 5.8% of revenue in FY26 to about 4.8% in FY27 and 3.7% in FY28 onward, adding roughly 1% of revenue a year, plus Rs 25-30 crore of one-off costs (Delhi property tax ex gratia, labour code) that drop out from FY27.
FY27 renovation spend about 1.9% of revenue, normal renovation thereafter at about 1.3% (possibly 1.0-1.2%); GST impact rising from 1% to 2% of revenue in FY27 as it becomes a full year.
Expected openings of about 2,000 rooms in FY27, rising to about 3,000 in FY28 and 4,000 in FY29; management says openings lag signings by about three years, with signings of about 5,000 rooms a year.

Lemon Tree standalone post-demerger: steady-state flow-through on management fees of 75-80%, currently about 60% pro forma; steady-state PAT about 60% of revenue (per management, after tax and no interest or depreciation).

Fleur targets up to Rs 3,000 crore of deployable capital over 12-18 months (including Warburg primary investment), and plans to add about 2,500 rooms; management does not give fee guidance for FY27-28.
Demerger: CCI approval received in April; SEBI and shareholder/creditor approvals underway; NCLT timing 6-18 months, with management giving 12-18 months as the outer limit.
Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt may rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, temporarily.
capex_capacity: Renovation: about 5,000 rooms to be renovated, of which 4,000 heavy renovation with about 85% complete; about 400-500 rooms under renovation in Q4 and similar in Q1.
Keys Whitefield renovation expected to complete in about 4 months; Keys Hosur Road under renovation; Keys Pimpri, Pune completed.
Aurika Naldehra, Shimla: 2 of 3 blocks to open by Q2 FY27 for the summer season.
Aurika Varanasi: 47-room heritage licence signed January 2026 on the ghat by the Ganges.

Nehru Place (572 rooms, North India's largest hotel) awaiting final approval before construction; estimated Rs 700 crore; Andaz (525 rooms) nearby, with cash flow over 3.5 years, 60% in the last 18 months.
Acquisition valuations cited at 8x-16x EBITDA; greenfield build 3-4 years, renovation-led acquisitions 1-2 years, operating assets immediate.
demand_pricing: Mid-March decision to prioritise occupancy over rate; April-May tactical pricing to keep an occupancy premium, with ARR roughly flat YoY; Q4 occupancy reached what management called a ceiling.

Corporate travel slowed in March as companies cut travel due to fares and the war; corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% from 59% in Q4 (negotiated room nights 55.4% for the full year vs 56.1%). Retail filled the gap at lower rates.
Indigo shutdown in December and the Middle East war (from early March, continuing into April) cited as headwinds; May described as surprisingly good.
Mumbai micro-market saw about 2,000 keys added in the last year (from Accor Fairmont to Ginger), creating a temporary supply glut for Aurika Mumbai.
Target: 65% of business from retail (direct, B2C, loyalty) once the portfolio reaches 20,000-25,000 operating rooms.
Loyalty programme has about 24 lakh members, driving about 25% of room nights per management.
Indian mid-market: management says demand outpaces supply; cites 2.5 million unbranded rooms in India as a conversion opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Would Fleur's inventory be managed by a non-Lemon Tree operator post-demerger, and how would that work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fleur is brand-agnostic and would choose whichever brand makes economic sense, while Lemon Tree should not be discriminated against; it cited a lost 5-star NCLT bid as an example.

qa_highlights.question: Why Aurika RevPAR growth (3%) lags Keys (16%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to micro-market differences and timing; full-year FY26 RevPAR growth was 19% for Aurika and 20% for Keys, with Keys set to keep growing as renovations finish.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you on conversion of signings into openings, and what fee numbers for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings lag signings by about three years; management declined to give fee guidance but expects about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-saving path and steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Renovation, GST and technology costs to fall to about 3.7% of revenue by FY28; pro forma Lemon Tree flow-through is about 60% now, targeted at 70%+ and then 75-80%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised demerger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CCI approval came in April; SEBI/shareholder/creditor steps underway; NCLT is the main variable, with 12-18 months the outer limit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did incentive-linked management fees lag for third-party hotels versus Fleur?
qa_highlights.answer: Incentive fees (1-5% of revenue depending on GOP slab) fell as renovation and GST cut owned-hotel EBITDA margins; third-party fees rose 23% from net additions, Fleur fees rose 8% on a same-store basis.

qa_highlights.question: What peak debt level is comfortable after Fleur's deployment?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-EBITDA about 2.25x now; consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore temporarily if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation for standalone Lemon Tree post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Lemon Tree to be debt-free and cash-generative; Board to decide a dividend or buyback policy; no F&B expansion planned, with a high hurdle for acquisitions.

risks_watch: NCLT timing for the Fleur demerger: management guides 6-18 months, with 12-18 months as the outer limit; CCI approval received in April, SEBI, shareholder and creditor steps still pending.

Demand softness: corporate share of occupancy fell to 55% in Q4 from 59%; March and April were weak on the Middle East conflict and airline disruption, though management said May was surprisingly good.

Margin recovery depends on renovation spend falling to about 1.9% of revenue in FY27 and GST impact and technology costs easing; standalone flow-through is about 60% pro forma versus a 70%+ steady-state target.
Openings execution: about 2,000 rooms targeted in FY27 versus 1,523 rooms opened in FY26; openings lag signings by about three years and owner-finance delays could cause slippage.

Leverage post-deployment: consolidated debt could rise to Rs 2,500-3,000 crore from about Rs 1,500 crore if Rs 1,500 crore is deployed, versus debt-to-EBITDA of about 2.25x now; Fleur's 2,500-room pipeline is not yet firm.
Aurika weakness: Q4 occupancy fell 2% after a large Mumbai wet-lease ended and Mumbai micro-market supply rose by about 2,000 keys; Keys RevPAR growth depends on completing renovations.

Tone on the Q4 softness was defensive, attributing weakness to Indigo, the war and Mumbai supply.

541233|2026-06.headline: Lemon Tree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs 346.8 crore, but net EBITDA margin fell 99 bps to 43.8% on GST and SAR provision.
541233|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 346.8 crore and PAT rose 19% to Rs 57.3 crore, while occupancy rose 314 bps to 75.7% as the company shifted to a volume-led retail strategy. Gross ARR rose only 2% to Rs 6,361 because retail business carries lower net ARR after commissions, and management called Q1 an aberration driven by West Asia-related corporate travel softness. Margin compression came from a GST input-credit loss and stock appreciation rights provision, worth 3.1% of revenue combined. Management expects Q2 to be better, with July described as strong and August as solid. The call also covered the planned demerger of Fleur Hotels and Warburg's Rs 960 crore investment in Fleur.

segments.name: Owned hotels (Lemon Tree)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 320 crore of network revenue, 56% of network revenue. Net EBITDA margin hit by GST input-credit loss and renovation spend of about Rs 9.8 crore (2.25-2.3% of revenue).

segments.name: Managed and franchised (asset-light)
segments.commentary: Contributed Rs 256 crore of network revenue. Opened 6 hotels with 334 rooms and signed 13 hotels with 1,020 rooms in Q1. Same-store managed revenue grew 9-10%.

segments.name: Keys portfolio (Fleur)
segments.commentary: RevPAR up 19% YoY to Rs 2,885, with occupancy up 350 bps to 67% and ARR up 13% to Rs 4,311. Renovation is about two-thirds complete across 7 hotels.

segments.name: Fleur Hotels (pro forma)
segments.commentary: FY27 revenue Rs 311.4 crore (+7%), net EBITDA ex-GST Rs 125.1 crore (+10%, margin 40.2%), PAT Rs 34.7 crore (+23%).

Management targets a long-term Lemon Tree EBITDA margin of 75-80% as fee income doubles and corporate costs fall as a share of revenue.
Management targets Keys EBITDA of Rs 60 crore on revenue of Rs 115-120 crore, implying Rs 6.5 lakh per key EBITDA.
Target of about 2,000 rooms opened in FY27; management says it is broadly confident, with Q1 at 334 rooms.
Renovation spend is expected to fall to about 1% of revenue from FY28. GST impact is about 2% of net revenue and expected to decline gradually.
Demerger of Fleur expected to complete in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in late second half of calendar 2027 after SEBI, shareholder, creditor and GST approvals.
Fleur's long-term plan is to keep debt-to-EBITDA around 2x; Fleur targets roughly 15% ROCE after renovations are complete.

Aurika Shillong (leased, 165 rooms): about Rs 33 crore deployed; opening expected H2 FY28.

Renovation: 300 rooms renovated in Q1 at about Rs 10 crore; similar number expected in Q2. Management expects 600-700 rooms in H1 and refurbishments of about 800 rooms in H2.

Fleur plans capital deployment of about Rs 2,500-3,000 crore, funded by Warburg's Rs 960 crore and about Rs 200-300 crore of balance-sheet cash. Management targets about 2,500 rooms of operating and under-development acquisitions.
Asset-light pipeline: 23,381 rooms across 279 hotels, of which 11,946 rooms across 135 hotels are operational.
demand_pricing: Q1 ARR growth was driven by a retail-led volume strategy, which lowered net ARR after commissions. Management calls this temporary and says the mix is returning to balance in July and August.

Corporate demand softened in high-density CBD markets such as Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru during the West Asia conflict, with lower travel, hiring and relocations. Delhi, Bengaluru and Hyderabad still outperformed; Mumbai and Gurgaon did not.
Mumbai airport micro-market absorbed about 2,000 new rooms over the last two years, creating a temporary supply mismatch. Aurika Mumbai pricing is being reset, with the stated aim of higher ARR.
Around 52% of company room sales are below Rs 7,500 (the GST threshold) and 48% above. Management is repricing demand-dense hotels to reduce GST drag.
OTA share of business is in the mid-30s%, and direct channels rose in Q1 with the retail push. Management expects a better negotiated versus non-negotiated mix from Q2.
Management says July was strong and August solid; Q2 demand is significantly better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is Keys' 19% RevPAR growth in line with the pre-renovation plan, and what remains to be spent on Keys renovation?
qa_highlights.answer: Keys is close to the Red Fox ARR target of about Rs 4,500 and is still a work in progress; management expects full performance next year with occupancy near Lemon Tree averages and reiterated a Rs 60 crore Keys EBITDA target. Remaining spend on about 300 rooms is about Rs 13-14 crore, at roughly Rs 4-5 lakh per key for second-tier Keys hotels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ARR grow only 2% despite Keys growth, and is the lower-ARR strategy continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the retail push to fill rooms during the West Asia-driven corporate slowdown lowered net ARR after commissions. It called this temporary, with a more balanced occupancy-ARR mix from July and August, and said Q1 was an aberration.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's Rs 2,500-3,000 crore deployment and Warburg's Rs 960 crore be done at peak-cycle prices, and what are the IRR expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry to deploy and that it is not in an up cycle, since India occupancy is in the mid-60s versus a 70-72% up-cycle threshold. It will focus on demand-dense top 6-7 cities, nearby 3-5 hour international markets and leisure locations, using brownfield, operating assets at 6-8x, greenfield and long leases, with returns targeted at about 60% post-fees ROCE and a conservative downturn assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 and FY28 net EBITDA margins recover, given the 47% analyst estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be well above 47%. It targets at least 50% in FY28 as renovation spend drops to about 1% of revenue and GST drag falls from about 2% of net revenue, with ARR rising 5-6% in Q2 and further in winter.

qa_highlights.question: Is Mumbai guidance being cut, and will Aurika Mumbai reach double-digit RevPAR growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was an aberration and that Q2 will be better, citing about 2,000 new rooms near the Mumbai airport. It said RevPAR is stabilised and the focus is now on repricing Aurika ARR, and declined to give a numerical RevPAR target before Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2,000-room opening target for FY27 slip, given 334 rooms opened in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slippage is normal in the business but it is broadly confident of about 2,000 rooms, based on the current pipeline and owner relationships.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net room additions lag the 334 rooms opened in Q1, and what was the management fee compounding outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tarudhan Valley (70 rooms) was terminated and Nestor (130 rooms, no fees) was removed, so fee-earning additions were lower. It said about 1,300 rooms were added year-on-year and that about 5,000 managed rooms signed in FY26 are due to open by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the renovation timeline, and how much margin was lost to renovation versus GST and SAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 renovation spend was Rs 9.8 crore (about 2.25-2.3% of revenue) versus a normal Rs 3 crore, and that about 300 rooms were done in Q1 with a similar number in Q2. It said refurbishments of about 800 rooms are planned in H2 and that the renovation drag disappears in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fleur's acquisition push raise debt above 2x EBITDA, and how will the debt be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt may briefly exceed 2x EBITDA during construction, with a long-term target near 2x. Fleur debt is about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; group debt is about Rs 1,275 crore after excluding about Rs 200 crore of cash. Warburg's Rs 960 crore will be deployed before listing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapil Sharma said CCI approval is done and SEBI and exchange scrutiny is in progress, followed by NCLT filing and hearings. Completion is targeted in H1 CY2027, with Fleur listing in the late second half of calendar 2027 as the conservative assumption.

risks_watch: Q2 delivery versus management's claim that July was strong and August solid; the Q2 ARR recovery of 5-6% and the balance of negotiated versus non-negotiated business are unverified until the next print.
GST input-credit loss persists at about 2% of net revenue; the pace of pricing above Rs 7,500 (52% of room sales currently below) determines whether the drag falls as guided.
Mumbai and Gurgaon corporate demand softness and the roughly 2,000-room Mumbai airport supply overhang; Aurika Mumbai repricing may not translate into RevPAR growth.
Execution risk on the ~2,000-room FY27 opening target (334 opened in Q1) and on managed-hotel friction, including terminations that reduce net room additions.
Fleur capital deployment of Rs 2,500-3,000 crore and the debt-to-EBITDA path, plus demerger approvals (SEBI, shareholders, creditors, GST, NCLT) that could delay the H1 CY2027 completion.
Renovation spend and margin recovery depend on the H2 refurb schedule (about 800 rooms) and on FY28 margin of at least 50%, which management itself called a stretch if not achieved.
key_quotes: But I would say this is temporarily; this was undertaken largely to react to the swing to the situation that we had in Q1.

541301|2026-06.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.

segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

541336|2026-03.headline: IndoStar Q4 FY26 net loss of INR424 crores on INR326 crores extra SR provision and INR49 crores West Asia overlay, despite 17% QoQ disbursement growth to INR1,306 crores.
541336|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a repair-and-transformation year: tighter underwriting, portfolio diversification away from MHCV, opex cuts under Project Leap, and legacy security receipt (SR) clean-up. Q4 disbursements rose 17% QoQ and 21% YoY to INR1,306 crores, and AUM reached INR8,056 crores, up 5% QoQ. Q4 was loss-making because of an additional INR326 crores provision on SRs, a INR49 crores management overlay for West Asia risk, and about INR55 crores of extra ECL charge from the annual model refresh. Management guided to a 3-year framework through FY29 with 35% disbursement CAGR, PAT of INR450-500 crores, and a loan book of INR16,000-17,000 crores.

segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements INR52 crores (+73% QoQ from INR30 crores) at 21.8% yield; AUM INR175 crores. Average ticket about INR7.5 lakh, LTV below 40%, tenure about 7 years; 1+ DPD at 0.3%. Live in 108 branches.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said stressed assets are largely provided for. SR net carrying value of INR589 crores is expected to be realized over about 18-36 months, with redemptions on large construction projects starting after 12-15 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the additional INR490 crore buffer (INR326 crores SR plus INR49 crores overlay plus about INR55 crores ECL refresh)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the SR provision as prudence, the INR49 crores overlay as an anticipatory West Asia buffer, and the ECL refresh as revised LGD and PD inputs. It said no stress is visible in the portfolio and that the overlay will be held for about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stage 3 aspiration, and is a 2-2.5% credit cost achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 3 is expected to settle at 3.75-4%, with a gradual decline through the year. Normalized credit cost is targeted at 2-2.25% once the old book runs off.

qa_highlights.question: Are slippages coming mainly from the older book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed. It said old-cohort delinquency is falling month on month across buckets and that bounce rates are declining.

qa_highlights.question: How is opex expected to behave with disbursements growing 35-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects opex to rise only marginally in FY27, with AUM and revenue growing much faster than costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR450-500 crore PAT target for FY27 or FY29, and does it assume a 2% credit cost and 9% funding cost?
qa_highlights.answer: It is for FY29. Management said it reflects the current 9% incremental borrowing cost and the 2-2.25% normalized credit cost, and that these are not base or worst case. Rating upgrade could lower funding costs further.

risks_watch: Credit quality: gross Stage 3 rose to 4.8% and Q4 slippages were high; the old book is still a large share until about September 2026.
Fuel price increases and West Asia crisis could hit SRTO and fleet customers; management has a INR49 crores overlay and says it would tighten policy if stress appears.
SR recovery timing (18-36 months) and the INR589 crores net carrying value depend on construction-project progress.
Growth ramp versus 35% CAGR target and 100-branch expansion; execution and cost discipline must hold while opex is kept flat.
Management declined to give Q4/Q3 interest reversal and NPA amounts on the call, so interest income flatness is not yet explained.

541400|2026-06.headline: Zim Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.2% YoY to INR 942 mn, but EBITDA margin fell to 3.7% and PAT was minus INR 40 mn, with EU-GMP outcome pending.

EBITDA was INR 34 million (3.7% margin) and PAT was minus INR 40 million versus minus INR 19 million a year earlier, as higher employee, utility, power and consulting costs weighed. Management said the EU-GMP reinspection (May 2026) is complete, the draft report has no critical observations, and the final report is expected within one to two weeks. Management guided FY27 growth of 10-15% without EU approval and a 30-35% jump in FY28 if EU-GMP and supplies start, but it kept the FY27 EBITDA margin near last year's level.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gross margin of 58.1% higher than the usual 55-56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product mix drove the Q1 level and the normal range is 55-58%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EU-GMP status, and are there major observations?
qa_highlights.answer: The draft report has no critical observations, but there are some major and minor ones. Management said the CAPA alone should be enough for recertification, with no reinspection.

qa_highlights.question: How quickly will sales follow EU-GMP approval, and what growth is expected in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about two quarters of lag, with supplies starting in Q4, and 30-35% FY28 growth with EU-GMP. Growth without EU is 10-15%. About 60-70% of growth is attributed to EU.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8-10 EU MAs need refiling if EU-GMP is delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: No refiling is needed unless the delay goes beyond three to four months. The MA depends on a valid EU-GMP certificate, and the 210-day procedure is near its end.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be double digit at about INR 500 crore revenue, and what are the non-EU economics?

541402|2026-03.headline: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin rose to 14.45% from 8.96% on 4% lower revenue; consolidated PAT turned to ₹6.97 Cr profit from a ₹11.65 Cr loss.
541402|2026-03.overview: FY26 was framed as a transformation year: management chose selective, higher-margin projects over volume, and standalone total income fell to ₹11,093 lakh from ₹16,069 lakh. Consolidated EBITDA swung to ₹1,716 lakh (14.19% margin) from a loss of ₹233 lakh, helped by about ₹151 lakh of GST provision reversal and ₹130 lakh of ODI loan interest in other income. Humro (ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary) secured a ₹48 Cr strategic investment, which will dilute ARAPL's holding below 50% once allotment completes. Management stopped giving numerical guidance, citing only a directional aim to beat FY26 "much much better".

segments.name: Automation (ARAPL, domestic)
segments.commentary: Welding lines for automotive OEMs such as Honda, Magna, Tata, Mahindra and Suzuki. Order book ₹4,496 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹2,696 lakh plus ₹1,800 lakh new bookings, per the presentation). Management said the verticals' combined book is about ₹127 Cr.

segments.name: Car parking (ARAPL)
segments.commentary: Multilevel parking, with customers including Lodha. Order book ₹820 lakh at 31 May 2026 (opening ₹580 lakh, new ₹155 lakh per the slide). Management plans to start exporting parking products in 6-9 months and to scale domestically.

segments.name: Warehouse automation (Humro / ARAPL RaaS, 83% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Mobile robots and WES for Fortune 50 customers; about 15 units and roughly $25,000 per month of revenue since December 2025. Order book ~$3 Mn (30-35 units, lease model, ₹36 Cr); outright-sale pipeline ~₹60 Cr. Target 225 robots in FY27, which management has not revised.

guidance_outlook: No numerical revenue or margin guidance; management said it has stopped giving number guidance and expects FY27 to be 'much much better' than FY26.
Humro FY27 target of 225 robots maintained; management said demand is 'much more' than supply.
Humro margin target of 15-18% on RaaS and outright sales, described as a moving target. Management said year-one EBITDA is not the focus; the aim is 15-20 good customers.
Next-quarter timing: Q1 is seasonally weak and profitability is expected from Q2 onward.
Humro pricing aim to cut prices by 50% over the next two years, with product-level price deflation.
ARAPL's first new product (exportable) targeted for mechanical completion in June/July 2026 and readiness by November/December 2026; radical growth expected in FY28.
capex_capacity: Five plants covering 350,000 sq ft; around 300 permanent staff and 100 contract workers (per the chairman's remarks).
Humro in-house manufacturing line: first product targeted by end-June 2026, a second model by August, and five products manufactured locally this year.
Humro inventory in the US is about 29 units, of which 5-6 are demos and 5-6 are in sales. About 20 units are to be commercially sold, with 12-15 already deployed.
FY27 deployment schedule: first 15 units ship around end-June/first week of July 2026 and a further 10 around 15 July, for deployment July-September; a further 50-60 units are being built.
Planned US strategic partner to hold local inventory, cutting delivery lead time from about 4 months to about 15 days.
demand_pricing: Humro's ₹36 Cr lease-model book equates to about $100,000 per month of lease rental; about $25,000 per month is currently billing, with $75,000 expected within one to two months.
Management said it is priced around 15-20% below Chinese competitors; named US competitors are Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav.
Management said the April-May 2026 Humro deployments were nil; 24 units were contracted and expected to deploy over the next couple of months.
Order timelines for automation work have slipped 6-8 months as customers deferred spending (per management), and some orders were rejected on profitability.

Domestic AMR opportunity: management says customers importing more than 500 AMRs from China into India are being targeted as a substitute. Management said it will not take low-margin India execution work.

qa_highlights.question: How many Humro robots were deployed in April-May against the 225-unit FY27 target, and is the target being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: No new installs in April-May; 24 units were contracted for deployment in the following months. Management said there is no revision to the 225-unit target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue fall sharply when the Q3 call indicated flat revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it rejected low-margin orders and added a cost-control department. Customers also deferred timelines by 6-8 months from February 2026 amid a global constraint, which delayed dispatch and revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does Humro compare with competitors on quality and price in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management named Vecna, Seegrid and VisionNav, saying they are about two years ahead. It claims pricing 15-20% below Chinese offers and cites technology, Indian software and easy integration as advantages.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ₹48 Cr investment will go to which uses, and what happens to ARAPL's holding?
qa_highlights.answer: The ARAPL holding is 83% now and will drop below 50% once allotment completes. Most funds go to operations and marketing, with some to product development; management said it does not plan local US manufacturing for now.

qa_highlights.question: Can minority shareholders still benefit after Humro is no longer a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARAPL will consolidate its share of around 43-45% of Humro profit, and that minority benefits are intact. No detailed structure was given.

541403|2026-03.headline: Dollar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore, but gross margin fell 169 bps to 28.1% on mix and cotton costs; price hikes of 4-6% planned.
541403|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 operating income grew 13.2% YoY to INR622 crore and volume grew 12.0%, but gross margin compressed 169 bps to 28.1% as the economy segment rose to 47% of revenue and cotton/yarn costs rose. Operating EBITDA grew only 2.0% to INR58 crore (9.3% margin), while PAT rose 11.4% to INR33 crore. For FY26, operating income rose 10.0% to INR1,881 crore, EBITDA 9.3% to INR200 crore (10.6% margin) and PAT 18.0% to INR107 crore. Management implemented a calibrated price hike in April (3-4%) and plans another 2-3% in June, and it deferred FY27 guidance to the Q1 call.

Management says the price hike has not hurt demand and that competitive intensity is stabilising; no market share loss is expected since peers are also raising prices.
Lakshya contribution to revenue was about 27% in Q4 versus 29% a year earlier, but management said the full-year contribution was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the price hike a one-off, how large is it, and does it come with scheme rollbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry-wide hike after about 2 years: 3-4% in April and 2-3% in June, total about 4-6% (CFO cited 6-7%). It is a pure price increase; schemes and discounts are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Can debt of INR264 crore be substantially reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt can be reduced to zero by FY28; about INR50 crore of short- and long-term borrowings were repaid last year. Management expects further cash from a 5-7 day cycle reduction.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 gross margin decline, cotton or competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mix (economy at 47%) and yarn costs were the main factors; prices were unchanged while realisation fell. Management denied meaningful discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the economy-segment shift structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is temporary, citing high demand in Tier 2/3 and rural areas, formalisation from unorganised players, and advertising of Dollar Lehar from the past three years. Force NXT grew 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin return to double digits and what is the FY27 growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 margins should be better than FY26 and it is eyeing double-digit growth, but gave no specific number and deferred guidance to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory and working-capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from about 130 to 100; management said optimised inventory is 95-100 days given the 90-day production cycle, and receivables are the main lever for the next 5-7 day reduction.

541403|2026-06.headline: Dollar Industries Q1 FY27: operating EBITDA up 11.4% to INR 48 crore at 11.8% margin, on price hikes and no discounting, while volume fell 1.6%.
541403|2026-06.overview: Operating income rose 1.4% YoY to INR 405 crore, with gross margin up 192 bps to 37.4% after a 4-5% calibrated price increase taken in April. Management chose not to match market discounting, so revenue growth was limited and volume declined 1.6% YoY, mainly from Dollar Man. PAT rose 22.1% to INR 26 crore and net debt fell to INR 192 crore from INR 277 crore at March 2026. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 11-13% and operating EBITDA margin of 11.5-12.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is quick commerce growth broad-based across products, and what drove the South region's strong growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed South growth to the Mahesh Babu brand association (signed about two years ago) plus better retailer placement and rising consumer acceptance. Quick commerce was about 5% of sales, growing 59% in value in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry price hike sustainable, and will the volume decline be recovered in the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects pricing and discounting to stabilise over one to two quarters. It targets double-digit volume-plus-value growth for FY27, with full-year revenue growth of about 11-12% internally and 11-13% guided.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and can it be sustained without further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Two drivers: the 4-5% price hike and not matching competitor discounts, which held revenue growth to about 1.5%. Management said low-cost inventory was a small contributor, as input prices rose from late February and the hike came in April. It sees no further hike needed as yarn and cotton have stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drove the volume decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Dollar Man volume fell about 3-3.5%, the main driver of the total 1.6% volume decline. Socks fell about 7% but are only about 2% of sales. Dollar Woman grew 1.5-2% in volume and Dollar Always was flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin benefit will come from the INR 100 crore advertising cap?
qa_highlights.answer: Ad spend was 7.7% of revenue in Q1. Management expects ad cost to fall to about 5% of sales from 5.5% last year at the 11-13% growth target, a benefit of about 0.5% of margin. Ad spend breakdown: about INR 100-102 crore a year across digital, TV, IPL, hoardings and in-store branding.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Lakshya Phase-2 mechanics, and why are no new states being added?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase-2 reactivates retailers, not distributors: 1,73,561 enrolled against about 80,000 active, with a target of about 90,000 active in FY27. No new states are being enrolled because each rollout disrupts a state for 5-6 months; UP and other large states remain for later.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cash conversion cycle and debt targets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CCC is 160 days; management targets a 6-7 day cut in FY27 vs March 2026 and 15-18 days over three years, reaching 130-135 days in three to four years. INR 86 crore of debt was repaid in Q1, and total debt (about 90% working capital) is targeted at zero by FY28. Q1 operating cash flow was about INR 96 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Force NXT and the G.O.A.T JV?
qa_highlights.answer: Force NXT grew about 7% in volume in Q1, but value declined as innerwear with lower ASP grew. Overall ASP is about INR 220. FY26 revenue was INR 85-90 crore (4.5% of sales), with 20-25% growth expected for the next 2-3 years. G.O.A.T's FY27 target is INR 75 crore, against about INR 50 crore in FY26.

The Board has appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen, with a conclusion expected in H1 FY27, and the polymers carve-out from CRAMS is on hold. Debt was cut by about INR 158 crores in FY26 to a line of sight of about INR 503 crores by end-May 2026, and management has an internal target of being debt-free by FY29. 541729|2026-03.headline: HDFC AMC FY26 profit after tax rose 16% to INR28.6 billion; QAAUM grew 20% to INR9.3 trillion and dividend of INR54 per share was recommended.
541729|2026-03.overview: HDFC AMC closed FY26 with revenue from operations of INR41.2 billion (up 18% YoY), operating profit of INR32.1 billion (up 18%, 35 bps of AUM) and PAT of INR28.6 billion (up 16%). QAAUM reached INR9.3 trillion (up 20%), with equity-oriented AUM at INR6 trillion and unique investors up 3.5 million to 16.7 million. Management highlighted record March 2026 SIP flows of INR321 billion industry-wide and said investor behaviour during the market correction was disciplined. The major open issue is the SEBI base expense ratio (BER) change effective April 1, 2026, which management expects to offset through commission changes with no material P&L impact.
