segments.commentary: Equity-oriented AUM reached INR6 trillion. Actively managed equity yield was about 60-61 bps, versus 56 bps including index funds.

segments.name: Debt and liquid funds
segments.commentary: Debt yield was 28 bps and liquid 13 bps in Q4. Management said the balance sheet debt book is run with modest duration and largely passive management.

segments.name: Alternatives, PMS and international
segments.commentary: Alternatives margins are marginally above equity margins, and discretionary PMS is in line with equity margins. Non-discretionary EPFO/SPFO mandates earn thinner net economics. GIFT City has five live funds, all wholly owned.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the gross impact of the base expense ratio change on existing book at about 3-4 bps, to be largely offset by commission restructuring and cost management, so targeted P&L impact is not material.
The 5 bps trail previously paid in lieu of exit load has been removed, and GST on management fees now sits outside the expense ratio, requiring margin adjustments.

No formal cost guidance is given. Employee cost ex-ESOP grew about 12.5% YoY, with five-year CAGRs of about 13% for employee cost and 13.5% for non-employee cost; costs are expected to grow broadly in line with business.
Management said flow market share is above book market share, and the company will launch SIF products only after careful design, not as a race.
Management said the SEBI-classified category presence is complete and new launches will be selective, with focus on sharpening existing funds.
capex_capacity: Physical branch network significantly expanded over the last couple of years, with further expansion under evaluation.
Investment in AI, cloud technology, cybersecurity and talent for PMS, international and alternatives; management called these foundational investments.
Rajan Anandan (Peak XV) appointed as invitee and external expert on the Technology Committee for a three-year term.
Seven new schemes launched in FY26, and first close of a private credit fund with IFC as partner and anchor investor announced.
Two EPFO/SPFO fixed income PMS mandates won. SPFO is already being managed, and the EPFO agreement is being signed.
demand_pricing: Industry: FY26 net inflows INR7.4 trillion, with equity-oriented funds about INR4.9 trillion; March 2026 SIP collections INR321 billion (up 24% YoY, 97 million contributing accounts). Industry market share is around 12.8-13% for the last eight to nine quarters.
HDFC AMC: direct plans about 31% of equity AUM; 97% of transactions digital; total accounts above 30 million; unique investors 16.7 million, up 3.5 million, versus industry addition of 7.2 million.
Unique investor penetration rose from 17.6% (March 2023) to 27% (March 2026). Folios rose from 2.3 crore to 3 crore, and SIP and STP flows were INR48.8 billion in March 2026 (up 33% YoY).

Management said flow share is higher than book share across channels, including fintech and HDFC Securities. HDFC Bank share of the distribution pie is declining, which management attributed to broad-based growth across other channels.
Competitive pressure: management stated SBI is almost closed-architecture, and some banks are more guided in retail distribution.

qa_highlights.answer: Gross impact on the existing book is about 3-4 bps, to be offset through commission optimisation and cost management, so no material P&L impact is targeted. New commission structures already reflect removal of the 5 bps exit-load trail, and the company will share more detail over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why does a third-party calculation show Q4 flow market share below Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the calculation missed IDCW (dividend) payouts in Q4 that were recorded as redemptions; the company does not accept the computed figure. Management said overall flow share remains above book share.

qa_highlights.question: Why has one-year scheme performance and industry ranking weakened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds remain in the top two quartiles across most categories and that many are rated 4 or 5 stars by Value Research. It pointed to long-term alpha track records, with 12-13 funds having 15-year-plus records.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY27 and FY28 expense growth targets available?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific guidance is given. Employee and non-employee costs have grown at about 13% CAGR over five years and are expected to grow in line with business and investments.

qa_highlights.question: What was the reason for the other income increase, and how is the balance sheet positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said balance sheet equity is mainly SEBI skin-in-the-game MF holdings, which saw drawdowns in Q4. The remainder is in liquid and debt funds with modest duration and passive management.

qa_highlights.question: Will HDFC AMC launch new NFOs or SIF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has secured all regulatory approvals for SIF. It is designing a couple of differentiated products but views the category as strategic rather than immediate. Management will stay selective on new launches.

541741|2026-03.headline: Fratelli Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR36 crores and EBITDA turned near breakeven at INR1.06 crores for FY26, with FY27 guidance of about 30% growth.

541770|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp recovery: AUM grew 14.0% YoY and 11.4% QoQ, disbursements rose 28.4% YoY to INR 8,313 Crore, and PPOP grew 23.1% YoY to INR 780 Crore. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 778 Crore (ROA 2.7%, ROE 10.7%), with credit cost at 6.74% versus 5.5-6.0% guidance, including 0.64% from ECL rate increases (INR 39 Crore extra in Q4 for West Asia-related scenarios). Competition in Tamil Nadu from peers entering individual loans; management argues execution and existing customer base (about INR 30,000 Crore already in portfolio, INR 40,000 Crore outside) are the edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 credit cost guidance so wide at 3.0-4.0%, and how much is from higher ECL provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Dalvi said the new ECL model (Stage 1 at 1.63%) already prices in global risks. The range reflects uncertainty over the West Asia fallout. April and early May PAR accretion is stable, so the company may land at the lower or higher end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-4% credit cost guidance conservative, given PAR accretion is under 10 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Narayanan said Q4 is normally the lowest-accretion quarter after an elevated credit cost period. The range also includes a normal one-month accretion rate, heatwave risk and external events.

qa_highlights.question: Will MFI growth shift toward individual loans, and is the 60-40 MFI/non-MFI mix a constraint over 10 years?

542011|2026-03.headline: GRSE posted record FY26: revenue INR 7,002 crore (+38%) and PAT INR 748 crore (+42%), with order book down to INR 15,324 crore.
542011|2026-03.overview: Management reported best-ever Q4 and FY26 results, with Q4 revenue of INR 2,119 crore (+29% YoY) and PAT of INR 303 crore (from INR 244 crore). Eight warships were delivered in FY26, including three on a single day, and the company said revenue from the bridges vertical crossed INR 200 crore for the first time. The order book fell to INR 15,324 crore, the first time it has dropped below INR 20,000 crore in five years, which management attributed to faster execution. The NGC corvette contract (~INR 33,000 crore, GRSE as L1) is still unsigned; management now expects signing in the June quarter, and it pushes NGC revenue recognition to H2 FY28.

qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the INR 18,900 crore figure reflects annual fund outflow, not intent. He cited AoNs, RFPs and approved Navy and Coast Guard roadmaps as evidence of continued focus.

qa_highlights.question: Relevance of conventional platforms versus autonomous vessels, and GRSE's strategy in autonomy.
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional platforms remain relevant for armament and endurance. GRSE has developed subsurface and surface autonomous vessels, supplied one to a DRDO organisation, and targets the XL AUV under Make projects in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the revenue in the 31 March provisional figure materially different from the final reported number?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had kept a conservative provisional figure because three ships were delivered on the last day. After formalising deliveries and revenue with the Navy, final revenue came to about INR 7,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NGC delayed, and when will it be signed? Will there be one or two winners on smaller projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Price negotiations are complete. Contract signing was expected by 31 March but is now expected in the June quarter, with no red flags. Smaller projects are mostly single-yard awards, with 120 FAC and P-17 Bravo split between two yards.

qa_highlights.question: When will NGC revenue start and how will revenue and EBITDA margins look for FY27-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: NGC revenue recognition starts in H2 FY28, with the major chunk from FY29. Margins are expected to be similar in FY27 and the company will try to maintain them in FY28-FY29. Management did not confirm no FY28 revenue dip.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY25 and FY26 margins inflated by provision write-backs, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Analyst cited 8.3% EBITDA margin in FY25 and 11.6% in FY26. Management said the current year margins will be similar but would not give a specific percentage, saying it is only Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NGC vendor ecosystem and electronics content?
qa_highlights.answer: Equipment and systems are ~65% of project cost; electronics is 55-60% of that and machinery and systems 40-45%. First downstream orders expected within three months of contract signing, majority within three to six months. BEL expected to be a key partner.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company take large European commercial orders and target higher margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commercial export projects will be selected for good margins. Warship projects, at ~INR 675 crore per ASW ship, still carry the best money and margins. Hybrid large vessels are being targeted.

qa_highlights.question: How are commodity cost increases handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Existing contracts are fixed price and vendor contracts are fixed price too, so no material impact was reported. Time delays on steel and industrial gas were marginal. New bids will factor in uncertainty.

542011|2026-06.headline: GRSE Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to ₹1,815 crore and PAT 44% to ₹173 crore; order book ₹13,596 crore.

The company said this was its 17th consecutive quarter of upward trend in financials. Order book stands at ₹13,596 crore across 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, and the Next Generation Corvette (NGC) contract is still awaited with management guiding signing within the quarter. Capacity expansion (brownfield and greenfield, roughly ₹4,200 crore combined capex) was the main strategic update, alongside Navratna status granted on 19 June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Does GRSE have capability for unmanned and autonomous naval vessels, and does the expansion plan address it?

It is taking part in Navy-steered autonomy projects and was shortlisted for another underwater unmanned platform.

Capacity goes from 32 to 43 platforms, including larger Aframax/VLGC-type vessels.

qa_highlights.answer: MR tankers and VLGCs are being bid with a sister yard and, for VLGC, a foreign yard with proven capability. Container ships are being pursued through a partnership with an Indian yard that has the dock and berth infrastructure, as GRSE lacks physical capacity for them.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 execution momentum be sustained, or will growth slow from the ~35-40% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current quarter's performance can be replicated, pointing to about ₹4,500 crore left on P-17 Alpha and about ₹1,816 crore on anti-submarine craft. It noted FY26 delivered eight ships and that the next quarter should see deliveries and higher contract workforce costs.

542216|2026-06.headline: Dalmia Bharat Q1 FY27 volumes rose 9% YoY while EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores; Jaypee acquisition closed at INR2,850 crore EV.
542216|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew 9% YoY despite state elections in key markets, and premium products reached 25% of mix. Revenue rose 7% YoY to INR3,890 crores and realisations improved 6% QoQ on price hikes of INR10-15/t in South and INR15-20/t in East. EBITDA per ton rose 3% QoQ to INR1,055, but absolute EBITDA fell 11% QoQ to INR805 crores on lower volumes and fuel/packing cost inflation. The Jaypee Cement acquisition (5.2 Mt cement, 3.3 Mt clinker, Central India) closed on 29 May 2026, with a INR182 crore exceptional charge for stamp duty and transaction costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Provisional, conservative estimate of stamp duty and incidental costs; final number expected by the end of next quarter, likely slightly better than provisional.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the exceptional item expensed rather than capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Dharmender Tuteja said that under business combination accounting, stamp duty does not add to fair-valued assets and is charged off; it is capitalised for tax and depreciation purposes.

qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Dalmia said 110-130 Mt is directional and can be calibrated; the 75 Mt target, earlier FY27, is now close in FY28, roughly a year behind, with capital allocation kept disciplined.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Weather365 premium offering is seeing strong response, but no new product launch date was specified; Konark brand is being phased out.

542323|2026-03.headline: KPI Green FY26 total income rose 56% to INR2,742 crore and PAT 57% to INR509 crore; management guides 40-50% growth.
542323|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income reached INR2,742 crore (up 56% YoY), EBITDA INR1,006 crore (up 73%) and PAT INR509 crore (up 57%). Q4 FY26 total income was INR810 crore, EBITDA INR305 crore and PAT INR155 crore. Installed capacity stood at over 1.62 GW with 4.64 GW under work-in-progress, and operating cash flow rose to INR424 crore from INR208 crore. Interest cost rose sharply (about 130% to INR182 crore) as IPP capacity was commissioned ahead of full revenue, and management defended the margin and ROE trajectory with FY27-28 as the inflection years.

segments.name: CPP / EPC

IPP capacity of about 1.7 GW targeted for commissioning in FY27 (DC basis), with the 250 MW and 370 MW projects due October 2026, the 150 MW wind project November 2027, and a 300 MW SJVN project awaiting PPA signature.

Land bank of 7,210 acres, of which about 800-1,000 acres is owned and the rest is held on 26-27 year leases.
demand_pricing: CPP order book about INR5,246 crore; management says this equates to roughly 2.7 GW, though the analyst's order-book reconciliation was not fully resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory of about INR1,400 crore is 30-40% of the order book, built to execute orders on time given geopolitical supply risk on turbines and panels.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter pledge timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of promoter shares are pledged against SBI's INR3,000 crore sanction. Release is tied to COD of the 250 and 370 MW projects, with full release expected by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Botswana funding and equity structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Botswana will be a step-down subsidiary under FEMA ODI rules, which allow investment up to 4x the parent net worth. Management says it has in-principle approvals from international funds for the equity portion.

qa_highlights.question: Grid stabilization charges in Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still evaluating project feasibility. It is not a rooftop player, and grid stabilization charges are not present in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income, depreciation and finance cost up so much?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income rose on fixed-deposit interest. Depreciation and finance cost rose with about double the asset base and higher working capital limits, following the FY25 QIP.

542323|2026-06.headline: KPI Green Q1 FY27 total income rose 16% YoY to INR710 crore and EBITDA 21% to INR262 crore, but PAT fell to INR95 crore from INR111 crore.
542323|2026-06.overview: Revenue and EBITDA grew, with EBITDA margin up to 37% from 35%, but PAT declined as depreciation and interest on newly commissioned IPP assets were booked upfront while revenue ramps. Management said billing delays on utility-scale EPC projects pushed revenue into the next quarter, and cited geopolitical cost pressure on steel, cables, logistics and cranes. Portfolio reached 6.94 GW (1.87 GW installed, 5.07 GW WIP). Management guided to 30-40% revenue growth (softened from the chairman's 40-50%) and a PAT margin below the earlier 16-18% for FY27. The CFO Salim Yahoo is leaving and Kapil Kriplani joins as Group CFO.

segments.name: IPP (Independent Power Producer)
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 2.57 GW; expected to generate more than 390 crore units annually at full run rate; management cites 85-90% EBITDA margin on IPP and 25-year PPAs. Management expects IPP revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW is at peak, with peak timing in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

segments.name: CPP (Captive Power Producer) / EPC
segments.commentary: Portfolio of 4.37 GW; CPP order book approximately INR5,000-plus crore. Management said EPC is about 83% of total revenue, and that margins were hit by higher costs for steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes.

segments.name: Sun Drops Energia (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Management expects Sun Drops to cross INR1,500-odd crore of top line in FY27 across IPP and CPP; Sun Drops IPO is mentioned as upcoming.

segments.name: KP Energy (EPC subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Per analyst, EBITDA margin fell from 22% to 12%; management attributed it to a pure EPC model with greater exposure to cost inflation and shared-cost absorption.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of 30-40% YoY for FY27, with management saying it is being conservative given geopolitical conditions; chairman had earlier spoken of 40-50%.
PAT margin for FY27 expected to be below the earlier 16-18% guidance; no specific revised number given.
Management expects the full earning contribution of new IPP assets to build through the rest of FY27, with most projects targeted for energization by September and full stabilisation in FY28.
Long-term debt to net worth targeted at a maximum of 3:1; management said leverage could rise to around 3x as project loans are drawn.

Annual interest cost for the full IPP capacity estimated at around INR450 crore (at about 8.5%); IPP depreciation estimated at about 5% on the building component, with total IPP capex potentially INR5,000-6,000 crore in FY27-28.
Botswana: 500 MW first phase under planning; management said no revenue from Botswana in FY27, with revenue in later years.
capex_capacity: Total portfolio 6.94 GW as of June 30, 2026 (up 71% YoY from 4.06 GW): 1.87 GW installed plus 5.07 GW work in progress.
Commissioned 0.85 GW and booked 2.88 GW of fresh orders over the year.
Land bank 8,657 acres; power evacuation capacity 5.10 GW; 133 sites total after entering Rajasthan.
BESS: 565 MW / 1,130 MWh project executed, financial closure under process.
Floating solar: 142 MW EPC order at Kadana Dam, Gujarat under execution.
150 MW wind for GUVNL: PPA signed and financial closure achieved; 300 MW SJVN-backed wind PPA signing under process.
Botswana: MoU with government for 5 GW; 500 hectares of land acquired (transcript corrected from 500 acres); PPAs at an advanced stage.
Energy trading licences from GERC (intrastate) and CERC (interstate); trading in pilot mode.
UAE: solar plus BESS project for a containerised data centre awarded to subsidiary Sun Drops Energia, under execution.
demand_pricing: Management said data centres are an emerging opportunity with inquiries ongoing, but no order share was quantified.
Growth slowed below guidance because utility-scale billing for customers such as Coal India, Adani Group and Aditya Birla Group slipped into Q2.

Geopolitical conditions raised costs of steel, cables, MMS structures, logistics and cranes; management said costs were partly absorbed and partly passed on to customers, and that sales were not affected.
Inventory built up at end-March to secure materials amid geopolitical disruption; it fell somewhat in Q1 and is expected to decline further as projects complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why was execution slow versus guidance, with growth of 16% against the 40-50% previously cited?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shortfall was billing timing on utility-scale projects, and that it is now guiding to 30-40% growth, being conservative due to geopolitical factors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the sharp fall in CPP and KP Energy gross margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed higher balance-of-plant, logistics and cost inflation from geopolitical conditions; KP Energy is pure EPC with about 17-18% of its revenue from IPP, so it was more exposed.

qa_highlights.question: Will IPP stay at a share of the revenue mix, and is the balance sheet strained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to keep IPP at about 20-odd% of revenue mix; leverage is 'below 3' and may rise towards 3x as loans for projects due by September are drawn, with EPS expected to recover as plants stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What are the annual interest cost, EBITDA and depreciation for the IPP business at full scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest is around INR450 crore a year at about 8.5% on roughly INR5,000 crore of debt; IPP EBITDA is 85-90% with revenue of at least INR1,000 crore once 1 GW peaks, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27; depreciation is about 5% on the building component.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 PAT margin meet the 16-18% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 and Q4 would recover only part of the Q1-Q2 gap, so the FY27 PAT margin would be lower than 16-18%; full benefit is expected in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: What was Q1 cash flow from operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Salim Yahoo estimated about INR140-150 crore, computed as PAT of about INR94 crore plus quarterly depreciation of about INR45 crore.

542337|2026-03.headline: Spencer's Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 6% YoY to INR436 crore, with Spencer's format up 8% and first YoY growth in many quarters.
542337|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 sales grew 6% YoY to INR436 crore, with EBITDA of INR2 crore against flat last year, and margin at about 18.8%. Spencer's format grew 8% to close to INR380 crore, with H2 growth of almost 4% and month-on-month growth reported since November. Full-year consolidated sales fell about 10% to INR1,800 crore after FY25 store and regional exits, and EBITDA was INR15 crore versus INR60 crore last year, which included one-off other income. Nature's Basket lagged, with management attributing its decline to internal issues such as inventory mix and supply chain problems.

qa_highlights.answer: Offline breakout not disclosed; growth driven by ABV, with NOBs flat. Online: 2.6 million orders in FY26 (about 2.15 lakh per month) at INR760 AOV.

qa_highlights.question: Nature's Basket turnaround measures after the leadership change.
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: consistent fresh availability (fruits, vegetables, chicken, meat, exotics), rebalancing excess processed, canned and imported stock, rewards expansion, and rebuilt online platform on Jiffy tech stack.

qa_highlights.question: Listing Nature's Basket on quick-commerce platforms.

rows.why: Management has outlined about INR30 billion of capex over FY27-FY29 with INR10 billion enabling debt approval, and Hyderabad (INR5,600 million construction) and Udaipur upgrade timelines are still undisclosed, so further project-level disclosures are expected; utilisation is not disclosed, but resort occupancy averaged about 43% for FY26.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides mid-to-high double-digit room revenue growth for FY27 on mid-to-high single-digit RevPAR growth and expects a strong H2 bounce-back as marriages return, with April stronger than expected, though the recovery is not yet quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 hospitality RevPAR fell 3% with occupancy down 7.7 pp and 10-12% disruption from West Asia, and management said June is only steady, so the H2 recovery case is largely qualitative.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Taj Delhi 70 rooms launch by Q4 FY27, Udaipur upper-upscale upgrade planned (timeline undisclosed), and Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad (330 keys, ADR around INR25,000) launch by end FY29.

rows.label: Net debt down to about INR19 billion from INR25 billion (Mar 2024)
rows.why: Net debt is about INR19 billion at March 2026 with a cash buffer of about INR4 billion, but planned INR30 billion capex is to be funded internally and a INR10 billion debt approval is enabled, so leverage could rise if capex is debt-funded.

rows.label: CRE leasing ramp toward INR300 million monthly rentals
rows.why: March 2026 rental run-rate is INR280 million with committed occupancy about 88%, and CIGNUS II commissioning in FY28 is expected to drive a step change; existing inventory is already above 90% occupied.

rows.label: Mumbai recovery and foreign-tourist return
rows.why: Mumbai ADR grew 0-2% in Jan-Mar 2026 vs India 6-8%, and March cancellations cost about 9,000 foreign-tourist room nights, so recovery depends on West Asia conditions.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2 FY27 recovery, CRE ramp and pipeline, but defensive and evasive on Mumbai weakness, Udaipur timelines and Hyderabad stabilisation; analysts pushed on the disruption, capex funding and margins.

542399|2026-06.headline: Chalet Q1 FY27 core revenue up 10% to INR5,140mn and EBITDA up 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%.
542399|2026-06.overview: Excluding residential, revenue grew 10% YoY to INR5,140mn and EBITDA rose 15% to INR2,400mn, with margin up 231bps to 46.7%; net profit was INR861mn. Hospitality RevPAR rose 6.5% on 8.5% ADR growth, with leisure resorts up 19% while FTA-dependent markets (Hyderabad, Bangalore) and MMR (Powai, Vashi) lagged. Commercial real estate revenue rose 18% to INR865mn with 85% margin, and the June 2026 rental run rate reached INR290mn per month. Management said August looks positive but declined to guide for the quarter given day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.change: Slightly up vs March 2026 after acquisitions

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR4,185mn (+9%) and EBITDA INR1,784mn (+11%), margin 42.6%. Leisure portfolio RevPAR +19%; Pune high double-digit RevPAR growth; Hyderabad and Bangalore weak on occupancy due to FTA decline.

segments.name: Commercial real estate
segments.commentary: Revenue INR865mn (+18%) and EBITDA INR735mn (+21%). Portfolio committed about 91%; LOI signed for 66,000 sq ft more at Bangalore; monthly rental guided to INR300-320mn during FY27.

segments.name: Residential (Koramangala)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 completed; INR73mn revenue and INR31mn EBITDA recognised this quarter. 168 Phase 2 units to be handed over during FY27. Prior-year comparison distorted by one-time recognition.

segments.name: MMR portfolio
segments.commentary: Powai and Vashi (over 60% of MMR inventory) lagged on construction and renovation; JW Sahar saw good ADR growth with steady occupancy. MMR is about 43% of hospitality revenue in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Planned capex of about INR30bn over FY27-FY29 across hospitality and commercial real estate, largely funded by internal accruals.
Monthly rentals expected to scale to INR300-320mn during FY27; CIGNUS II Powai commissioning to drive step-change from FY28.
Taj Delhi Airport: minimum 70 rooms to launch in Q4 FY27, balance in phases within Q1 of next fiscal.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by FY27 end.
South Goa hotel construction expected to start by end of the current quarter, after the rainy season.
Management declined to guide for the quarter; August described as overall positive, September too far out.
capex_capacity: Hospitality portfolio to exceed 5,000 keys; management targets adding 500+ keys every year.
Added 129 keys at Bangalore; Dukes Retreat rebranded to Athiva with 67 additional keys.
Udaipur (Athiva) expansion awaiting approvals from local authorities and army cantonment; clarity expected in one to two quarters.
Mindspace projects at Hyderabad and Airoli have begun excavation; both on track.
CIGNUS II Powai adds 0.9mn sq ft of office space; INR10,914mn of net debt allocable to under-construction or yet-to-be-operational assets.
demand_pricing: Leisure resorts occupancy about 51% this quarter; management sees stabilised resort occupancy at 60-65%.
Athiva Khandala weekend rates sustained above INR15,000; weekday MICE demand still needs building.
Powai porch and Westin banquet connectivity due by quarter end; noisy construction to end in one to one and a half quarters.
FPS (Fairmont-adjacent MMR asset) renovation done at INR93 crore; rebranding to be announced in coming weeks.
Management said supply in MMR has been absorbed, with no major new supply expected in the next one to two years.
Commission rates paid to OTAs and GDS described as bottom-end of the market; OTA and transient mix fell but management said this is not a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for MMR underperformance, booking window, MICE, and competition including Fairmont near JW Marriott Sahar?
qa_highlights.answer: JW Sahar outperforming on ADR with steady occupancy; Powai under construction and FPS renovation driving near-term pain. Supply absorbed with no major supply in next one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will leisure reach 20% of portfolio target change, and Inder Residency expansion potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy unchanged: leisure stays at about 20% of portfolio. Udaipur expansion awaiting two approvals; no firm number yet; existing building work proceeding.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for resort occupancy to reach 70%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Resorts stabilise at 60-65%; Q1 was 51% and expected to keep improving. Athiva Khandala creating a premium MICE market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8.5% ADR growth from pricing or channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: No major channel mix change; special corporate rates were raised slightly to retain them, and crew business increased.

qa_highlights.question: July trends and current outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Quarter started strongly, but visibility has worsened as the West Asia situation changes every 5 to 10 days. August looks positive; no quarterly guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term MMR occupancy ceiling, can it return to 77%+?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes Powai and FPS can return to prior levels and go beyond. FPS was at about 140% fair share before refurbishment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: FTA arrivals stay flat; management said normalisation takes about 60 days after resolution, and sentiment has deteriorated again.
MMR: Powai and Vashi occupancy recovery depends on construction ending and the porch reopening in H2 FY27.
Bangalore relocation and group business softness; Hyderabad FTA exposure.
Leisure occupancy may be partly driven by domestic shift from outbound travel; management says the 60-65% target is a given but timing is uncertain.
Goa and Udaipur project timelines depend on local and army approvals.
Net debt rising with acquisitions; INR10.9bn tied to assets not yet operational.
542399|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic and leisure demand and long-term Powai and resort upside, but cautious on the near term. Management repeatedly declined to give quarterly guidance or precise timelines, citing day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict and pending approvals.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has set a good tone for the full year. Overall performance has been strong despite challenging geopolitical situation.
The shortfall in foreign arrivals was offset by robust MICE demand, reflecting both the resilience of our portfolio and our ability to pivot quickly to existing demand.
So we continue to work on the same strategy as we have always had, 20% of our portfolio should be leisure, and we'll stay in that space.
Overall, this quarter, it would be remiss of me to give you any sort of guidance, because we are ourselves monitoring the situation on a day-to-day basis.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Taj Delhi Airport minimum 70 rooms launch in Q4 FY27 with balance in Q1 FY28, CIGNUS II Powai (0.9mn sq ft) substantial completion by FY27 end, and 129 Bangalore keys already added; hospitality guided to exceed 5,000 keys with 500+ added yearly.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Resort occupancy at 51% expected to keep rising toward a stabilised 60-65%, Bangalore added 129 keys and Dukes Retreat 67 keys, and commercial rentals rising from INR290mn to INR300-320mn per month during FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR30bn capex over FY27-FY29 already outlined and South Goa construction to start by end of current quarter; Udaipur expansion awaits approvals with clarity in one to two quarters, so further project-level announcements are probable though utilisation is only 51% in resorts.

rows.why: Management declined to guide for the quarter and August is only described as positive; visibility worsened as West Asia situation changes every 5-10 days, so no upgrade is firmly on the table.

rows.label: MMR recovery at Powai and Vashi after construction ends
rows.why: Powai and Vashi (over 60% of MMR inventory) lag on construction; porch reopens and noisy construction ends in one to one and a half quarters, while FPS was at about 140% fair share before refurbishment.

rows.label: Bangalore commercial LOI for 66,000 sq ft
rows.why: LOI signed for 66,000 sq ft more at Bangalore, with commercial portfolio already about 91% committed.

rows.why: Net debt INR20,405mn in June 2026 is slightly up after acquisitions, with INR10,914mn tied to assets not yet operational, though cost of finance eased to 7.4% from 7.5%.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic leisure demand, JW Sahar ADR and long-term Powai upside, but cautious near term and declined quarterly guidance citing West Asia volatility and pending approvals; analysts pushed on MMR underperformance, pricing versus channel mix and July trends.

542459|2026-03.headline: Kranti Industries crossed ₹100 crore consolidated revenue in FY26 (+28%), with standalone PAT of ₹260 lakh versus a ₹75 lakh loss in FY25.
542459|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described by management as transformational: consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore for the first time, and the company returned to profit. Standalone revenue rose 30% to ₹93.88 crore, with EBITDA up 63.7% to ₹1244 lakh and margin improving from 10.5% to 13.3%. Q4 standalone revenue of ₹29.31 crore was the highest quarterly figure on record, up 60.2% YoY and 28.2% QoQ, though Q4 EBITDA of ₹167 lakh reflects startup costs at the new Jaipur plant. The company also entered defence machining via AVNL orders and took over a Jaipur plant on lease from 1 January 2026.

segments.name: Agriculture / tractors
segments.commentary: Management described tractors as the major revenue source; agriculture was about 95% of revenue five years ago at around ₹20 crore. Management said non-agri diversification now stands at about 16%.

segments.name: EV components
segments.commentary: EV-related components contributed about 5.3% of FY26 revenue across Kalyani Techno Forge (one passenger-car EV part, one production line running for about 12-15 months), Dana group and Eka Mobility.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Entered defence via machining orders from AVNL in FY26. Management is targeting PSU customers directly rather than as a Tier-2/3 supplier; the company expects it to take 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position.

segments.name: Jaipur plant (Plant-4)
segments.commentary: Fourth facility, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity, with commercial operations from 1 January 2026. Utilisation was below 40% in its first quarter, and FY27 revenue guidance is ₹12-14 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit YoY revenue growth from here, subject to no extraordinary events.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 18-20% at about 85% utilisation with a richer product mix, targeted for FY28 rather than FY27.
Plant-4 Jaipur revenue expected at ₹12-14 crore in FY27.
Priorities for FY27: ramp Jaipur utilisation, expand exports, deepen presence in defence, industrial, construction equipment and EV, and improve working capital efficiency.
No immediate acquisition planned, but inorganic growth remains part of the Vision 2030 roadmap.
capex_capacity: Jaipur facility (Plant-4) commissioned; commercial production from 1 January 2026, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity.
Jaipur plant, machinery, instruments and business were taken on lease, with an exclusive arrangement under which the counterparty routes 100% of its machining through Kranti.
Pune facility utilisation is about 65%; management sees 80-85% as the maximum optimised level, leaving roughly 35% headroom.
Continued investment in CNC machining, automation and quality systems.
Management did not state a specific capex figure for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cited steady domestic tractor growth over three years and recovering European and American agriculture demand as tailwinds.
Supply chain and inflation pressures from the ongoing war were noted; management said customers are supportive and solutions are being worked on.
Defence sales depend on lengthy PSU tendering processes, which management said slows order flow.
China Plus One sourcing and localisation are cited as demand drivers for the company's precision components.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Kalyani Techno Forge relationship and EV revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: One EV passenger-car component has been supplied to KTFL for 12-15 months on one production line; further volumes are under discussion. EV components were about 5.3% of FY26 revenue, covering KTFL, Dana and Eka Mobility.

qa_highlights.question: Is there distress in rural demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; domestic tractor demand has grown for three years and European and American agriculture demand has started to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Pune utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Pune is at about 65% utilisation against a practical maximum of 80-85%, leaving about 35% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from the Jaipur Plant-4?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-4 utilisation was below 40% in its first quarter, and management expects ₹12-14 crore of revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Jaipur acquisition add?
qa_highlights.answer: It gives entry into the northern auto-ancillary belt, a ready plant with business, and a dedicated customer who will route 100% of its machining to Kranti under an exclusive agreement.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can defence scale and what is the approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting PSU customers directly, not as a Tier-2/3 supplier, and expects 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position because of the tender process.

qa_highlights.question: Where will EBITDA margins settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 18-20% EBITDA margin at about 85% utilisation, reached by FY28 rather than FY27.

risks_watch: Jaipur ramp-up: utilisation was below 40% in Q4, and Q4 EBITDA was only ₹167 lakh.
Defence order flow is slow and depends on PSU tendering; management expects 4-6 quarters before a substantial position.
Supply-chain disruption and inflation from the ongoing war; management gave no quantified impact.
Customer concentration: the Jaipur plant depends on one customer under an exclusive arrangement; EV exposure is only about 5.3% of revenue.
Margin target of 18-20% is aspirational and is pushed to FY28, against 13.3% in FY26.
542459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on long-term growth, Vision 2030 and diversification. Candid that Q4 margins and defence ramp-up are still in investment phase, and gave no quantified FY27 revenue guidance beyond the Jaipur figure and a generic double-digit growth view.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a transformational year for Kranti Industries and a significant milestone in our Vision 2030 journey.
We expect double digit growth year on year from here because that is going to happen unless and until something extraordinary does not happen.
However, my experience in this segment is a bit slow so to penetrate and to have a substantial hold on that, it will take another 4-6 quarters at least.

542484|2026-03.headline: Arvind Fashions Q4 FY26 revenue up 14.8% to INR1,365 crore NSV; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion.
542484|2026-03.overview: Q4 NSV rose 14.8% YoY to INR1,365 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income at INR189 crore (vs INR159 crore) and a 50 bps margin gain. Reported PAT was INR47 crore against a loss of INR93 crore a year earlier; comparable PAT grew 56%. For FY26, revenue grew 14%, EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 13.4%, comparable PAT grew 62% to INR124 crore, and ROCE crossed 23%. Direct channels reached 56% of sales, and management guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps margin expansion in FY27 despite macro and commodity risks.

segments.name: Retail (offline)
segments.commentary: Q4 retail grew 14% with LTL of 7.8%; PVH brands were hit by a transitory GST slab change to 18% for a few weeks, now back to double-digit growth. FY26 added over 1.4 lakh net sq ft; 50 EBOs added in Q4.

segments.name: Online B2C
segments.commentary: Grew over 40% in Q4, raising share to 14% from 11%, as the company shifts away from B2B online. Management expects online B2C to sustain 20%+ growth over the years.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: USPA posted its highest-ever growth in Q4; PVH brands and Flying Machine each grew over 10% (Flying Machine retail LTL in double digits, B2C up 70%). Arrow was subdued due to a one-time model change and weak wedding calendar.

segments.name: Adjacencies (footwear, innerwear and others)
segments.commentary: Adjacent categories grew 25% and now make up about 24% of business. Stride has 19 stores.

segments.name: Wholesale and department stores
segments.commentary: Delivered strong double-digit secondary sales growth in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27: sustain mid-double-digit revenue growth, with management citing about 15% and about 7-8% like-for-like growth split roughly equally between price and volume.
FY27: 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion, guided despite a more uncertain macro.
Net-debt-zero target now in about 9-12 months; apart from the Flipkart-related borrowing, debt is expected to fall year-on-year.
Store additions: about 1.5 lakh net sq ft of space expected in FY27; around 5% of stores expected to close going forward.
Longer term: take gross margin toward the high 50s over 2-3 years; take D2C share of sales to 65%.
Each brand expected to have its own dotcom and app live in FY27; flyingmachine.com to launch in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR110 crore, covering store investments including deposits for about 50 COCO stores opened in the year, MBO and department store investment, and IT and admin spend.
FY26 added more than 1.4 lakh net sq ft of retail space; FY27 plans about 1.5 lakh net sq ft addition across the portfolio.
Company reorganised into a business unit structure and set up a dedicated tech and AI team over the last two quarters.
Inventory turns expected to move to 3.7-3.8x from 4.0x as channel mix shifts toward D2C.
demand_pricing: Demand environment described as stable; government measures on GST, interest rates and income tax supported demand; West Asia situation flagged as a watch item.
Management expects mild pressure on raw materials, forex and capex, and a possible consumption slowdown from supply-led inflation; SS26 inventory bought early to lock costs, AW26 being hedged.
Management says sourcing remains predominantly India-based and will be deepened; selective price increases planned while protecting growth.
Premiumisation trend seen across all brands quarter on quarter; online competition described as stabilising.
Store closures expected at about 5% going forward, not concentrated in one brand.

qa_highlights.question: Will U.S. Polo keep growing at its recent pace, and how will brand-wise growth look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said U.S. Polo has reached its potential, PVH brands will keep growing, and Flying Machine should sustain solid double-digit growth. It guided to mid-double-digit growth across brands rather than a brand-specific CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Can 30-40 bps margin expansion hold with cotton prices rising and A&P spend increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India-based sourcing, cost-control measures, selective price increases and mitigation already in motion. It said it is cautious but optimistic on the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventory days up about 20 days over two years, and how many COCO stores were closed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed inventory days mainly to channel mix shift toward D2C, which holds inventory on books. Early SS26 inwards were made ahead of geopolitical delays, and creditors offset part of the build. The CFO did not have the COCO closure count and offered to follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to fund debt reduction and what is the acceptances position?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose in the quarter due to borrowing for the Flipkart transaction. Cash generation will go first to term loan repayment, then to working capital financing; acceptances are used to manage MSME payables and are reported in the annual report.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% retail LTL for the full network or COCO only, and how is it measured?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said LTL is based on consumer data across the full network. The company operates on a consignment basis for its stores, and sales are recorded when the final consumer buys.

risks_watch: Inventory rose more than 30% YoY in FY26 against 15% revenue growth; inventory days are up about 20 days over two years, and management attributes this to channel mix and early inwards.
Raw material, forex and capex pressure from the West Asia situation and cotton price uptrend could hit the 30-40 bps margin guidance.
Possible consumption slowdown from inflation; management has not quantified price increase elasticity.
Arrow subdued in Q4 (one-time model change, weak wedding calendar); the brand's recovery is still to be proven.
Flipkart transaction borrowing lifted debt in Q4; net-debt-zero target in 9-12 months depends on cash generation.
Reserves fell about INR13 crore YoY due to an equity adjustment linked to the Flipkart transaction.
Disclosure gaps: no brand-wise numbers, no full-price sales mix, and no COCO closure count given.

Our D2C engine is compounding. Direct channels now account for 56% of sales, up 300 basis points year-on-year.
Our brands have actually premiumized while at the same time ensuring great value at fabulous prices.

542484|2026-06.headline: Arvind Fashions Q1 FY27 net sales rose 15.5% to INR1,279 crore and EBITDA rose 19.6% to INR160 crore, with margin up 44 bps.

Gross margin rose about 90 bps to 56.7% on lower discounting and higher full-price sell-through, while marketing spend rose about 50 bps. PAT fell to about INR10 crore from INR13 crore, mainly because other income was lower. Management reiterated mid-double-digit revenue growth and 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion for the rest of FY27, while flagging West Asia-linked cost and forex pressures as a watch item.

542580|2026-03.headline: Aartech Solonics FY26 revenue reached Rs 40 Cr (record), with EBITDA roughly 3x FY25 as FY25 carried a ~Rs 4 Cr exceptional charge; order book guided to Rs 25 Cr by June 2026.
542580|2026-03.overview: Management held its first virtual investor call for Q4 and FY26 and described FY26 as a record-turnover year with tighter expense control. Revenue was stated as Rs 40 Cr for 2025-26, with organic growth of about 12-15% a year and roughly doubled over five years. EBITDA and PAT were said to be about 3x FY25, which included an exceptional expense of about Rs 4 Cr. Management discussed new export wins (Indonesia BTS, Qatar and Oman, China and Africa for control and relay panels), defence trials, and a new Narmadapuram facility targeted for operations in early FY28. Specific Q4 quarterly figures were not given in the call.

segments.name: BTS 2000 (Bus Transfer System)
segments.commentary: Flagship product serving process industries, refineries and gencos; average margin stated at 35-40%. Life cycle moving from new supply to retrofitting. Won Indonesia project against ABB.

segments.name: Control and Relay Panels (CRP)
segments.commentary: Traditional bread-and-butter line since the 1980s; now moving into volumes via EPCs, but price-sensitive with tough margin competition. Exports started to China and Africa; plan to enter 220 kV market.

segments.name: Defence (AAPM, EMLS, rugged mil-grade)
segments.commentary: AAPM validated across Northern, Western and Southern Army commands; patent filed, expected in 12-18 months. Orders executed for Indian Navy and Air Force. Management sized the market at Rs 500 Cr+ and an addressable Rs 50-100 Cr for Aartech.

segments.name: Ultracapacitors (Faradigm subsidiary), Flywheel, Kranking, BestCase
segments.commentary: Ultracapacitors manufactured through subsidiary Faradigm Ultracapacitors. Flywheel still in development, with traction in data centres. BestCase industrial plastic enclosures serve retail through B2B.

guidance_outlook: Order book expected to reach around Rs 25 Cr by end of June 2026, from Rs 10 Cr at start of FY26 against ~Rs 15 Cr of bids outstanding.
New Narmadapuram renewable and power equipment facility: civil work in progress for 9-10 months; first operations expected early 2027, commercial operations targeted end FY27 or early FY28.
Management declined to give a numerical revenue, EBITDA or CAGR target; said it prefers to under-commit and over-deliver.

Management expects organic growth in the 12-15% range to continue based on recent trends.

qa_highlights.answer: Margins vary by product. BTS 2000 at 35-40% tapers to 10-15% net across competitive products. Innovation is seen as the leverage, with a pipeline of R&D investments.

segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 156 lakh in Q1 per management. Ultracapacitor and energy storage programmes for the Army, with technical evaluation taking about 18 to 24 months.

Management described the quarter as the highest Q1 e-commerce revenue and PBT/PAT since listing, with new verticals (EPR, TReDS, travel) still awaiting regulatory or government go-aheads.

542650|2026-03.headline: Metropolis Q4 FY26 organic revenue grew 14.7% to INR 392 crores, with organic EBITDA margin at 27.2%, up from 18.5%.

Organic EBITDA margin rose to 27.2% (from 18.5%) and full-year organic margin reached 25.9%, up about 140 bps after adjusting for prior-year acquisition costs. Management said the heavy lab and centre build-out is largely done, so the focus shifts to throughput-led productivity, and it guided to 14% to 15% revenue CAGR and a 27% to 28% group EBITDA margin over three years. Core Diagnostics reached a high-single-digit margin in Q4, meeting the 4-quarter turnaround commitment.

Two large SDV programs ending; management expects the revenue gap to be covered by new accounts, with FY27 sequential growth of 4-5% lost versus the prior plan.
India revenue (about 4% of total) expected to roughly double in FY27; medium-term target of double-digit annualised growth.

Beacon AI platform used internally across about 13,000 staff and licensable as a product.

OEM spend outlook: McKinsey data (Jan 2026) shows automotive R&D spend growing about 2x by 2030, led by AD/ADAS (about 3x); management said its addressable share is smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap to cover in FY27 from the 4-5% sequential growth lost to program ramp-down?

qa_highlights.question: How does KPIT compete with Chinese automotive engineering firms that run lower margins?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 TCV jump, and is that repeatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor said the jump came from off-highway commercial wins and traditional clients; Sachin said quarterly variability is normal but half-yearly and yearly TCV is growing.

qa_highlights.question: Do European and North American OEMs plan to increase SDV spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin said European OEMs are focused on cutting cost and reconsidering partners, creating opportunities, while US OEMs are investing in next-generation SDVs.

542651|2026-06.headline: KPIT Q1 FY27: constant-currency revenue grew only 0.1% YoY and fell 3.6% QoQ, with EBITDA margin at 17.2% and PAT at INR 1.17 billion.

Profitability fell more than proportionally: EBITDA margin was 17.2%, EBIT margin 12.3%, and PAT INR 1.17 billion, hit by forex losses and a share of losses from Qorix tied to postponed European revenues. Deal wins were USD 257 million, led by connected cars, aftersales transformation and autonomous. Management guided H2 better than H1, with a return to growth by Q4, and said margin recovery will largely follow revenue recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 22% to 24% margin aspiration for FY29 from the Analyst Day still hold?

qa_highlights.question: Can you unpack US growth between OEMs and off-highway, and is the momentum sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Will the Europe impact show up in Q2, and what is the Europe revenue quantum?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said Europe impact was about 4% of quarterly revenue, will show up in Q2 at a regional level, and will be offset by US and SIMA growth at company level. He said SIMA dropped sharply this quarter off a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply this quarter, and what is the margin trajectory for the next three quarters?

542652|2026-03.headline: Polycab Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 27% YoY with EBITDA margin at 13.1% and record quarterly PAT of INR 7.9 bn, while Cable & Wire volumes grew only low single digits.
542652|2026-03.overview: Management reported record annual and quarterly revenue, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 27% YoY and PAT of INR 7.9 bn (up 7%, 8.9% margin). Growth was price-led: cumulative price hikes of 18-19% were taken from January to March, while Cable & Wire volumes grew low single digits in the quarter. Middle East escalation, PVC price spikes and pollution-related construction halts hit March, which is the key month of Q4. FY26 was a record year: revenue above INR 285 bn (+29%), EBITDA margin 13.9%, PAT above INR 27 bn (+32%), and FY26 volume growth of 18%.

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 30% YoY, with domestic cables up 30% and combined volume growth in low single digits. EBIT margin was 13.1%, and Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+. Cables outpaced wires, and institutional sales grew faster than channel.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 47% YoY, the ninth straight quarter of outperformance versus industry. EBIT margin was 4.1%, and FY26 EBITDA margin was mid-single digit. Solar was the largest FMEG category, growing 2x; premium fans were about 25% and premium lighting about 35% of segment revenue.

segments.name: International (exports)
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY and contributed 4.4% of consolidated revenue in Q4. Full-year export share was 5.4%, and Middle East was about 16% of FY26 exports, which was hit during the quarter.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue fell 15% YoY to INR 5,098 mn on project execution timing. Segment profit was INR 386 mn, a 7.6% margin. Sustainable margin is guided at mid to high single digits.

Management says there will be no scenario where Polycab runs out of capacity over the next 4-5 years.

FY26 Cable & Wire volume growth was 18%, versus industry growth of 11-12%, with domestic wires and cable organised market share at 30-31% (up 300-400 bps over FY25's 26-27%).
Channel is about 90% of business and institutional about 10%; channel margins are 3-4% higher than institutional. Institutional mix was 2-3 points higher in Q4.
Demand sectors: power 40-45% of cables, manufacturing and private industry 35-40%, mobility 10-12%, energy and exploration 5-6%.
Power capacity additions in FY26 were about 55-56 GW, nearly double FY25; management expects demand to defer by weeks, not be lost.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Cable & Wire volume growth and price hikes taken from January?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined volume growth was low single digits, with cables ahead of wires. Cumulative price hikes were about 18-19% from January to March.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the Middle East disruption in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary sales were hit as distributors lifted less, since secondary sales did not move at the expected pace. Private sector demand was hit by gas rationing, and PVC prices rose 60-80% in early March. The impact was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional mix and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutional sales were about 2-3 points higher than channel in Q4 (about 13-14% of the Cable & Wire top line in Q4 per management's arithmetic). Channel margins are 3-4% higher.

qa_highlights.question: Peak utilisation and capacity headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 75-76%. Management says early 90s has been reached at times, but 80-85% is the sustainable level, and there is room for growth.

qa_highlights.question: Use of surplus cash and M&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains on capex funded from internal accruals and on the dividend payout. M&A is being evaluated in India and abroad, but nothing is in view for the near to mid term.

qa_highlights.question: Export outlook for FY27 and the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a firm number, but expects exports to exceed the current 5.4% share. US distribution was re-established and North America was about 40% of FY26 exports. Middle East was about 15-16% of FY26 exports and is not expected to contribute meaningfully in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory gains and raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there are no inventory gains or losses because raw materials are hedged for copper and aluminium, and copper is largely imported. XLPE and compound availability is comfortable for about one quarter, with a diversified vendor base.

qa_highlights.question: Segment EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable & Wire Q4 EBITDA margin was around 14%+, and above the 13.9% company level for FY26. FMEG was mid-single digit for both Q4 and FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume growth outlook and market share?

qa_highlights.question: Is the data-centre and T&D demand strong enough to move industry growth, given the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 1 GW of data-centre additions alone would be limited, but said T&D demand is accelerating, with about 15% cable content in T&D spend and transformer makers' order books at about 2.5x revenue.

542652|2026-09.headline: Polycab Q2 FY27 revenue rose 53% YoY with PAT of INR 9,900 million (+43%) and EBITDA margin of 14.4%, all record highs.
542652|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-yearly revenue and profitability, with consolidated revenue up 53% YoY and all segments contributing to growth. EBITDA rose 39% YoY to a 14.4% margin, up more than 50 bps QoQ, helped by mix, operating leverage and copper price pass-through. Wires and Cables grew 47% and FMEG grew 124%, with FMEG crossing a 10% EBIT margin for the first time. Management said the Asier Metals IBC matter is under NCLAT review, with order reserved and no material impact expected.

financial_highlights.value: Growth 53% YoY (value not stated in call)

financial_highlights.change: Up more than 50 bps QoQ; EBITDA +39% YoY
vs INR 29.4 billion a year ago
Aided by higher payable days from increased letters of credit use

segments.name: Wires and Cables
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% YoY; domestic W&C +50% YoY with mid-to-high single-digit volume growth. Wires grew early double digits in volume and cables mid single digits. EBIT margin 14.2%, up sequentially. Exports grew 17% YoY and 85% QoQ, and were about 5% of revenue.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue +124% YoY, 11th consecutive quarter of industry-leading growth, and seventh consecutive profitable quarter per CEO. EBIT margin 10.1%, first time above double digits. Solar (inverters only, traded) was the main driver; fans premium mix about 33% and lights about 38%.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 6,171 million (+53% YoY), EBIT INR 444 million (7.2% margin). Order book about INR 9,000-10,000 crore, mainly Bharat Net and RDSS projects. Medium-term margin guidance is high single digit.

guidance_outlook: Wires and Cables medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 11% to 13% reiterated; management said it would be happy to run at the higher end.
FMEG target of growing 1.5x to 2x industry growth with margins; long-term EBITDA margin range of 8% to 10% cited for FY30.

Copper prices up about 6% QoQ and about 40-45% on average in H1; pricing is cost-plus with pass-through to customers (monthly for cables, fortnightly for wires).
UltraTech's entry into wires: management said no pricing action taken so far and no channel pricing correction seen.
Export order book strong in US, Europe, LATAM, Asia and Middle East; now selling to 94 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Are FMEG margins and the Wires and Cables margin rise sustainable, and would Project Spring targets be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited scale, operating leverage, premium mix and bundled solution offerings for FMEG. Targets are FY30-based; long-term FMEG EBITDA margin of 8-10% is still cited, and a 10.1% EBIT margin is described as very high.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pricing response to new wires entrants like UltraTech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no action on pricing so far, that the entrant's wires presence is a small share of the business, and that the company gained 1-1.5% share annually (3-4 points last year).

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be soft on a high base, and what is FY volume growth expected to be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly comparisons are not the right lens; the anchor is 1.5x market growth, and volume should be viewed on a 10-12 month basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a seasonal copper-price related inventory build or delay in offtake?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant pickup in channel inventory; copper rose about 6% QoQ and aluminium fell, and restocking follows price moves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 12.5 billion line in the cash flow statement?
qa_highlights.answer: It is advance payments for inventory procurement, not a one-off, roughly INR 1,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Q2 revenue run rate be sustained into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide revenue, noting copper price movements drive the base and demand is strong.

542665|2026-03.headline: Neogen Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 247 crore with 17.8% EBITDA margin; FY27 standalone guidance INR 875-950 crore.
542665|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 247 crore, almost entirely volume-driven, with EBITDA up 21% to INR 44 crore and margin at 17.8% despite Dahej replacement and toll manufacturing costs. PAT was INR 11 crore for the quarter and INR 29 crore for FY26 on revenue of INR 862 crore. Battery materials (Neogen Ionics) remain the core growth push: Dahej Phase 1 is budgeted at INR 428 crore and Pakhajan Phase 2 revised to INR 1,367 crore, with commissioning now guided within FY27. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue guidance at INR 875-950 crore, excluding battery sales, and separately guided INR 300 crore-plus from battery chemicals, weighted to H2.

financial_highlights.value: INR 14.6 crore inflow vs INR 246.1 crore outflow

segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 194 crore, up 7% YoY. Bromine derivatives about 40-45% of revenue, advanced intermediates about 30%, organolithium and lithium the balance.

Battery chemicals revenue guided at INR 300 crore-plus for FY27, mostly in H2 with sequential growth each quarter; excludes commodity price upside.

Electrolyte commercial manufacturing targeted for H1 FY27; electrolyte salt in H2 FY27. Dahej Phase 1 (1,000 tons balance plus 500 tons intermediate) targeted by Q3 FY27, with SCOD of February 2027 approved by lenders; Pakhajan Phase 2 SCOD March 2027.

FY28 tentative target of around INR 1,100 crore plus at full utilisation for the standalone business; FY28 battery revenue expected INR 1,200-1,400 crore by management estimate; FY29 consolidated revenue of INR 3,700-4,200 crore cited (standalone INR 1,200-1,250 crore plus battery INR 2,500-2,900 crore).
Targeted ROCE of 18-20% on the revised battery capex.
Commercial electrolyte supply from Dahej expected by July or August 2026 after completing audit corrections.
Morita equity contribution of USD 20 million expected in H1 FY27; management says funds from promoter (INR 161 crore) and JV plus insurance are sufficient to complete projects.
capex_capacity: Dahej Phase 1 budget INR 428 crore, completion targeted February 2027; Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion March 2027. Revision reflects Morita technology alignment, a 500 MT intermediate lithium salt addition and localisation of components.
Pakhajan electrolyte plant completed mechanical assembly and entered trial run; 30,000 tonne electrolyte plant under trial production, built on Mitsubishi technology per management.
Salt and additive capacity at Dahej: 5,500 tonnes total (about 4,000 tonnes salt and 750-1,500 tonnes additive), plus 500 tonnes intermediate over and above.

Remaining FY27 capex around INR 600-700 crore for Neogen Ionics plus about INR 100 crore for Neogen; no major capex planned for FY28 at present. Neogen Ionics gross block expected INR 1,700-1,800 crore at end-FY27; standalone gross block INR 450-550 crore.
Organolithium capacity raised 2.5x to 300 tonnes per year from about 120 tonnes; management expects 80-90% utilisation this year and a small capex possible next year.
demand_pricing: Lithium carbonate around USD 24-25/kg versus management's long-term stable band of USD 15-25 (centre about USD 20); management does not factor commodity upside into guidance because it is passed through.
Bromine prices elevated but stable after shipments from Dead Sea Bromine; contracts limited the Q4 impact. Management budgets bromine at about INR 300 plus or minus 50.

Chinese LiPF6 salt pricing was 30-50% below Neogen's formula price at start of the year; the gap is now about 20-25%. Electrolyte pricing guided at USD 6-8/kg (current lithium price about USD 7-9/kg), with USD 7-7.5 as average.

Two electrolyte customers have qualified Neogen; two more are validating Neogen electrolyte against Chinese electrolyte; two more start in 2027. Management says US electrolyte makers' site audits are complete with commercial clearances pending.
The domestic giga-factory customer is expanding from 1 GWh to 5 GWh in H1 2026 and is currently sourced solely from Neogen.

qa_highlights.question: Has the capex increase (over INR 250 crore) reduced battery project ROCE from the expected 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE should remain at 18-20% after revision, citing raw material savings, and that the added 500 MT intermediate capacity is a further source of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone trade payables stretch to nearly 365 days, and will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to longer supplier credit terms negotiated during the fire, some supplier factoring, and expects debtors and creditors to converge over 2-3 years as insurance money arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the peak debt changing after the capex increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak debt will remain as earlier at about INR 1,700 crore because INR 160 crore promoter equity and USD 20 million JV equity cover the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower Q4 inventory a sign of a problem, and what drove the rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose because of rented outside capacity winding down in March 2026 and Dahej not being online, so stock was built for Q1-Q2 sales.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank moratorium cover interest and principal?
qa_highlights.answer: Moratorium is for principal only, running one year from the revised commercial operation start date; interest is charged from COD and interest during construction is included in project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2,500 MT Dahej capacity on Morita technology or Neogen's own?
qa_highlights.answer: Most Dahej capacity is Neogen's own technology, with Morita adjustments made mainly at Pakhajan; the additive salt line has no Morita tie-up.

risks_watch: Project timelines slipped once: Dahej start moved from Q1 to Q3 FY27 due to construction labour shortages, and the capex was revised upward again; the commissioning dates are a key test.
Revenue delivery depends on Pakhajan and Dahej start-ups, approval cycles, and customers moving from China-sourced electrolyte; management has excluded Q4 Pakhajan revenue from its base case.
Lithium and bromine price volatility, plus Middle East-related supply chain and input cost pressure on packaging and logistics.
Trade payables at very high levels and working-capital normalisation expected only over 2-3 years; insurance receivable INR 203 crore net outstanding, with final settlement pending.

542665|2026-06.headline: Neogen Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR 250 crore, EBITDA up 53% to INR 48 crore, with margin at 19.3%.

EBITDA rose 53% to INR 48.2 crore and margin expanded 260 bps to 19.3% despite Dahej rebuild, toll manufacturing and Neogen Ionics start-up costs. PAT rose 67% to INR 17.1 crore. rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bokaro colour-coated line (1,50,000 t) is in hot trials with capitalisation and commissioning expected from Q2 FY27, and cold rolling and Galvalume lines follow with full ramp across about 6 quarters through FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Rolling mill is at 83.5% utilisation with demand-driven volumes, pipes and tubes rose from about 34% to 40.1%, and Bokaro throughput of about 0.5 million t starts in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 83.5% in rolling mill (above the 80% threshold) but the Bokaro downstream lines are already committed, so a fresh capex is not guided; pipes and tubes is at 40.1%, which argues against new pipe capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give FY27 or Q2 numbers and reiterated FY25-FY28 guidance unchanged, with Q1 revenue up only 11.6% YoY against a ~70-75% revenue CAGR target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Bokaro ROCE ramp

rows.why: Talks are under way to add gas price indexation to price variation mechanisms after fuel costs hit margins, but nothing is agreed yet.

542726|2026-03.headline: IndiaMART Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to Rs 404 crore, but paying suppliers fell 1,200 QoQ amid pricing pressure and elevated Silver churn.
542726|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 14% YoY to Rs 404 crore in Q4 and 13% to Rs 1,569 crore for FY26, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 133 crore (33% margin) in Q4. Net profit fell to Rs 50 crore in Q4 because of a Rs 34 crore mark-to-market loss on treasury bonds, versus Rs 475 crore for the full year. Paying suppliers rose 3,200 in FY26 to 2.2 lakh but declined 1,200 in Q4, which management attributes to a Silver tier price increase at the end of Q2 and the war that broke out in late February. Management gave no net-add guidance and said it is not reversing pricing.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 133 crore (33% margin) / Rs 530 crore (34% margin)
Negative Rs 34 crore, driven by treasury mark-to-market losses

segments.name: IndiaMART standalone
segments.commentary: Collections from customers were Rs 546 crore in Q4 (+8% YoY) and Rs 1,674 crore in FY26 (+10% YoY).

segments.name: Busy Infotech
segments.commentary: Q4 billing was Rs 45 crore and FY26 billing Rs 170 crore; normalised growth excluding the payout structure change was 24% in Q4 and 43% for the year. Q4 revenue was Rs 34 crore (+53% normalised) and FY26 revenue Rs 119 crore (+44% normalised); deferred revenue was Rs 124 crore (+44% normalised).

segments.name: Export business
segments.commentary: Management said export collections are now Rs 60-70 crore, versus Rs 50-60 crore earlier and Rs 20-25 crore when the business was purely domestic.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for double-digit growth in the near term, driven by ARPU growth of about 8-9% and paying-supplier growth of about 1-2%.
No guidance on net adds until multiple quarters of sustained improvement; management said churn must improve before gross adds can translate into net adds.
Management said it will not roll back pricing, and expects gross adds to normalise only slowly.
Dividend of Rs 60 per share declared (final Rs 30 plus special Rs 30), subject to shareholder approval; management will revisit the payout approach next year.
Management said Platinum and Gold customers are about 50% of the customer base and more than 75% of revenue.
capex_capacity: No capex figure, capacity metric or commissioning timeline was disclosed on the call; the discussion covered platform and product levers rather than capital spending.

Busy Infotech: 11 thousand new licences sold in Q4 and about 45 thousand in FY26, taking the total licence count to 4 lakh 42 thousand; AI-led features are being added to the Busy product, with no timeline given.
Platform headroom: management sees about 2x supplier headroom over the current 0.25 million paying base, and says about 80% of buyer product and location needs are already met on the platform.
Headcount is 6,200 with no planned rationalisation; campus hiring continues periodically to scale servicing and sales teams, and management said current staffing is at the required level.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries were about 27 million in Q4 and declined about 1% YoY; management attributed the drag to added buyer verification, which it estimated cuts traffic-to-enquiry conversion by about 1%.

Paying suppliers were 2.2 lakh at FY26 end; Q4 decline of 1,200 was attributed to a Silver price increase at the end of Q2 and the war that started in late February. Management estimated the war cost about 1,000-1,500 gross adds and pricing about 1,000-1,500.
Silver churn is elevated: about 7% monthly and about 4% annual, versus 5-6% monthly previously. Platinum churn is well under 1% a month, and Gold is 1-1.5% a month.
Registered buyers rose 9% YoY while active buyers fell 3% YoY, which management linked to agentic and bot traffic and new OTP verification.
Management said price increases apply only to new subscribers, so ARPU uplift is gradual over 1-3 years; revenue is recognised on an 18-month moving average.
Management said about 80% of buyer product and location needs are already met on the platform, and sees a 2x supplier headroom versus the current 0.25 million paying base.

qa_highlights.question: When will gross adds recover to support a net-add trajectory of 5-6% annually, and how much of the weakness is due to the war versus pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no net-add guidance. It estimated the Q4 shortfall at roughly 3,000 customers versus a positive trend, split between the war and the price increase, and said February-March normally perform better.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a vicious-cycle risk given flat or declining enquiries and buyers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the risk and described the business as at a plateau on an S-curve, needing a new product-market-fit lever to lift buyer frequency and supplier retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth going to be the main growth driver, and what are the VAS and credit options?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to rely only on ARPU, with customer and ARPU growth both needed until supplier count nears 4-5 lakh. Export is Rs 60-70 crore and logistics and credit are still pilots.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ARPU flat despite price hikes, and why did employee expenses decline QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes apply only to new subscribers and roll out over 1-3 years, and revenue uses an 18-month moving average. The Q4 employee expense decline reflected a Rs 8.5 crore labour code charge taken in Q3; headcount is 6,200 with no planned rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise payout or move to buybacks given cash generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40-60% of cash generated has been distributed over the last three to four years, and the Board chose a Rs 60 dividend, with a re-evaluation next year. Buybacks were deemed no different from dividends for now.

risks_watch: Elevated Silver churn (about 7% monthly) and slow gross-add recovery, with no net-add guidance.
Enquiry growth has stalled at 27-28 million per quarter despite performance marketing, and buyer verification may reduce conversion further.
Traffic and discovery risk from AI and chat platforms, though management said B2B enquiries are not yet declining.
Treasury mark-to-market losses from rising bond yields, which hit Q4 other income by Rs 34 crore.
Busy Infotech's normalised growth depends on the payout structure change; watch the Busy billing trend and AI feature rollout.
542726|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the long-term platform and cash position, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the near-term supplier and buyer trends. But we are not going back on pricing.

rows.why: Price increases apply only to new subscribers and revenue uses an 18-month moving average, so the ARPU benefit builds gradually while management targets ARPU growth of 8-9%.
