rows.why: Export collections rose to Rs 60-70 crore from Rs 50-60 crore earlier and Rs 20-25 crore when purely domestic, a steady upward trend.

rows.label: Busy Infotech licence and billing momentum
rows.why: Busy sold 11 thousand licences in Q4 and about 45 thousand in FY26 (total 4.42 lakh), with normalised Q4 revenue growth of 53%, but this depends on the payout structure change and AI feature rollout timing is not given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the platform, cash position and 40-60% payout history but defensive on supplier and buyer trends, blaming the war and pricing with no recovery timeline; analysts pressed on gross-add recovery, the vicious-cycle risk from flat enquiries, and ARPU versus supplier growth.

542726|2026-06.headline: IndiaMART Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 414 crore with 35% EBITDA margin, while paying suppliers fell by 1,850 QoQ to 2.18 lakh.
542726|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew about 11% YoY to Rs 414 crore and EBITDA was Rs 146 crore (35% margin), supported by lower customer acquisition spend and operating leverage. Collections grew 8% to Rs 463 crore and deferred revenue grew 16% to Rs 2,014 crore. Paying suppliers fell by a net 1,850 in the quarter to 2.18 lakh, driven by weaker gross additions and elevated Silver-tier churn. Management said buyer enquiries were flattish at about 26-27 million, with roughly 4-5% of the decline attributed to new OTP verification; it also flagged BUSY billing growth of only 10% (about 30% normalised) and a new finance subsidiary.

financial_highlights.change: Driven by mark-to-market gains on treasury portfolio
Net decline of 1,850 in the quarter

segments.name: IndiaMART marketplace
segments.commentary: Platinum and Gold subscribers are about 50% of the customer base and more than 75% of revenue, with good upsell and retention per management. Silver monthly churn was about 7%, unchanged per management.

segments.name: BUSY Infotech
segments.commentary: Billing about Rs 59 crore (+10% YoY); revenue from operations Rs 36 crore (+47%); deferred revenue Rs 146 crore (+44%); cash from operations about Rs 16 crore. About 12 thousand new licences sold, taking the cumulative count to 4.54 lakh.

guidance_outlook: Management said BUSY normalised billing growth is about 30% after removing a one-time Rs 10 crore win-back benefit in Q1 FY26; normalised revenue/deferred growth seen at 30-40%.
Over the next couple of years BUSY CAGR is expected at 27-30%; longer-term aspiration is 35-40% CAGR.
BUSY licence growth targeted at 15-20% in the next year or two as the business migrates from licensing to subscription.
Paid buyer programme is an experiment; management said free buyer access will remain free.
Segmented verification and churn containment expected to show results after about a year.
capex_capacity: Board approved creation of wholly owned subsidiary IndiaMART Finance Limited for short-term transaction financing via partnership lenders; management said no large lending from own balance sheet.
Advertising spend of about Rs 7-8 crore per quarter, targeted at top 10% monetisable categories; expansion to Meta, Instagram and YouTube planned.
AI voice call centre handles over 1 lakh calls per day, up from about 80 thousand manual calls per day previously.
Follow-on investments in Bizom, Fleetx, SuperProcure and Aerchain; management cited a 10% per-company limit on follow-ons.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries about 26-27 million, flattish QoQ; analyst cited an 11% decline and management attributed about 4-5% of the decline to OTP verification.
Active buyers down about 5%; about 40 million total active buyers, of which about 10 million are GST or verified business buyers.
Management described a shortage of enquiries as quality improved; 90-day buyer repeat rate at 58-59% (up from 50-51% over the years).
Management is pursuing category-based pricing and tiered pricing for Platinum plans.
Management said Google traffic is under pressure from LLM tools; LLM traffic attribution is not yet measurable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the purpose of IndiaMART Finance Limited and will it lend from its own balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Objective is transaction financing via partnership lenders for short-term products; no plans for large lending from own balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Why have collections in BUSY grown more slowly this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY26 included about Rs 10 crore of one-time win-backs; excluding that, growth is about 30%, with deferred and recognised revenue growing 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the buyer count declining and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut low-quality buyers earlier and now targets higher-ARPU categories with about Rs 7-8 crore per quarter of advertising; organic buyer decline partly linked to Google-to-LLM traffic shift.

qa_highlights.question: What initiatives beyond sales process changes will curb churn and improve gross adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Better supplier quality, catalogue and category curation, buyer quality via fill-rate, and credit embedded into transactions through the finance subsidiary.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the enquiry decline is due to verification versus traffic migration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 4-5% of the decline is from OTP verification; management could not quantify the rest, which may include LLM migration or macro factors.

qa_highlights.question: Are follow-on investments and new stakes planned given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Follow-ons continue on merit in Bizom, Fleetx, SuperProcure and Aerchain; no fixed rupee target was given and new strategic investments are limited.

risks_watch: Paying supplier base fell by 1,850 QoQ; Silver monthly churn at about 7%, with first-12-month cohorts the main problem.
Buyer and enquiry volumes are flattish to declining, with Google-driven acquisition under pressure from LLM tools.
Earnings are boosted by Rs 107 crore other income from treasury mark-to-market gains, versus Rs 146 crore EBITDA.
BUSY billing growth of 10% reported, with normalised growth around 30%; license growth is about 10%.
Watch the rollout of IndiaMART Finance Limited and the buyer paid programme, and whether gross supplier additions recover.

key_quotes: Margins continued to be elevated on account of savings arising from lower customer acquisition and operating leverage.
Now there is a shortage of buy leads or shortage of enquiry.
Most of the churn or retention problem is limited to the first-year onboarding itself.
We do not have any plans to lend out of our own balance sheet any large amount.

rows.why: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 35% on Rs 414 crore revenue, helped by lower customer acquisition spend and operating leverage, but Rs 7-8 crore per quarter of advertising is being redeployed toward higher-ARPU categories and Platinum tiered pricing is still being developed, so the gain is not locked in.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity is discussed; the AI voice call centre already handles over 1 lakh calls per day versus about 80 thousand manual calls before, so the capacity gain has already happened rather than being planned.

rows.why: Unique business enquiries are flattish at 26-27 million, active buyers are down about 5%, and paying suppliers fell by a net 1,850 to 2.18 lakh, so volume growth is not visible near term even though BUSY licence growth is targeted at 15-20%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; the only new spend is the IndiaMART Finance Limited subsidiary with no large own-balance-sheet lending and follow-on investments with no fixed rupee target.

rows.why: Silver monthly churn is about 7% and the first-12-month cohorts are the main problem, while 4-5% of the enquiry decline is from OTP verification and the rest from LLM traffic shift, which management could not quantify; segmented verification fixes are only expected to show results after about a year.

rows.why: Paid buyer programme is described as an experiment and tiered Platinum pricing and category-based pricing are being pursued, with expansion of advertising to Meta, Instagram and YouTube planned, but no launch dates were given.

rows.why: Q1 FY27 other income of Rs 107 crore was driven by mark-to-market gains on a Rs 3,553 crore treasury, which are non-recurring and flatter net profit of Rs 172 crore versus Rs 146 crore EBITDA.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, BUSY deferred revenue (+16% consolidated to Rs 2,014 crore) and AI initiatives, but cautious and at times evasive on buyer and enquiry declines, churn timing and LLM traffic impact, while analysts pressed on the 11% enquiry decline and the BUSY growth slowdown.

542726|2026-09.headline: IndiaMART Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore, with EBITDA margin of 37% and paying suppliers down 615 QoQ to 2,17,000.
542726|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 10% YoY to Rs 429 crore and consolidated collections grew 9% to Rs 443 crore, while deferred revenue rose 16% to Rs 2,029 crore. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 159 crore (37% margin) and net profit was Rs 91 crore, with other income negative at Rs 8 crore due to bond-yield MTM losses. Paying suppliers fell by 615 QoQ to 2,17,000, attributed mainly to elevated Silver subscription churn. Management said unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined for about two quarters, which it linked to AI-driven search changes and its own decision to restrict data access, with a 10-15% loss from peak levels.

financial_highlights.change: Due to MTM losses from bond yield increase; management calls it notional

segments.name: IndiaMART marketplace
segments.commentary: Collections Rs 394 crore (+8% YoY) standalone; 27 million unique business enquiries in Q2; paying suppliers 2,17,000 after net decline of 615 in the quarter. Gold and Platinum are about 50% of customers and about 75% of revenue.

segments.name: BUSY Infotech
segments.commentary: Revenue from operations Rs 37 crore (+27% YoY), billing Rs 46 crore (+20% YoY), deferred revenue about Rs 155 crore (+40% YoY), cash from operations about Rs 12 crore. About 11,000 new licences sold in Q2, taking the total to 4,66,000.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 33% reiterated; management called it conservative, and Q2 margin was 37% on a consolidated basis.

Management said margins are not comparable quarter to quarter because costs are upfront and revenue recognised over up to 18 months; it plans to invest more heavily in sales once Silver churn is better understood.
Management expects value and volume growth to be balanced over the next 2-3 years, versus historically about 10% value and 10% volume growth.
BUSY said comparable growth from Q3 onwards should be in line with the 20-30% overall growth rate it has been seeing.
No guidance on when Silver churn will improve; management has stopped giving that guidance.
capex_capacity: Management said 100% of expenses, including manpower and AI research, are expensed; no subsidiary capitalises manpower or software costs.
Advertising spend running at Rs 8-9 crore per quarter, nearing a Rs 10 crore per quarter budget, focused on the top quartile of categories.
Pilots underway for credit facilitation (IndiaMART Finance) and a paid verified business buyer programme; no significant capital committed yet.
Next ESOP pool decision to be taken by the board at financial year end; last pools were in 2018, 2022 and 2025.
demand_pricing: Unique business enquiries and active buyers have declined YoY for about two quarters; management attributes 10-15% loss from best-ever highs to Google AI Overviews and to restricting proprietary data behind logins.
Management said ARPU growth has historically run 5-10% and revenue growth is now 8-10%; growth has come mostly from value (ARPU and upsell) rather than volume over the last two to three years.
Silver 12-month retention is about 10% lower than four to five years ago, which management cites as the main gap to 10% volume and 10% value growth.
Around 10% of buyer traffic now comes through paid advertising, with 20-40% cannibalisation of organic traffic depending on the area.
Trust Assurance programme protects buyers up to Rs 5 lakh on purchases from verified bank accounts and TrustSEAL suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Why are active buyers and unique business enquiries declining, and is GenAI search a factor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: AI Overviews now cover 50% or more of searches, causing a 10-15% decline from peak. It has put more data behind logins and stopped showing some proprietary data to search engines and LLMs, and it accepts losing 10-20% of current enquiries to protect data.

qa_highlights.question: Is IndiaMART moving toward a transaction marketplace, as JustDial reportedly aspires to?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not going fully marketplace or away from listings, but wants to get closer to transactions, citing its earlier Tolexo and payment platform attempts and its current credit facilitation work.

qa_highlights.question: Where is AI showing up in the business, and is it monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 20+ AI use cases and voice AI serving 80,000-100,000 buyers daily, and said benefits are cost, intelligence and time. It said net benefit is volatile over 2-4 years and it does not expect AI to show up directly in enquiries yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ESOP cost fall, and what is the outlook for personnel cost leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Jitin Diwan said ESOP expense declines each year under the graded design, and the current level is the baseline until the next pool. Management said near-term AI experimentation adds cost and savings are reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the lending and credit facilitation business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to support marketplace transactions for high-value equipment, not to become a lender. Pilots are small and will be reported quarterly; no pre-approved credit lines yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for BUSY collection growth, which has appeared to decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Brijesh Agrawal said Q1 and Q2 FY27 growth was inflated by a higher base from a billing methodology change and customer win-back in the prior year; comparable growth should be 20-30% from Q3.

risks_watch: Paying supplier base declined by 615 QoQ; Silver churn has not yet improved and no timeline is given.
Unique enquiries and active buyers are down 10-15% from peak, with AI search and data restrictions cited as the drivers.
Other income is negative (Rs 8 crore) from bond MTM losses; management expects reversal over the next few quarters.
Credit facilitation and buyer monetisation programmes are at pilot stage with undefined capital and first-loss exposure.
Margin of 37% in Q2 reflects low sales investment; management plans to step up sales spend, which could compress margin.

542752|2026-03.headline: Affle 3i Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.3% y-o-y to INR 7.24 billion; FY26 revenue INR 27.1 billion (+19.5%) and EBITDA margin 22.5%.
542752|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 7.24 billion grew 20.3% y-o-y and 1% q-o-q, marking a 13th consecutive quarter of sequential growth despite geopolitical softness. EBITDA was INR 1.61 billion (22.3% margin, broadly flat y-o-y margin), and PAT was INR 1.20 billion (+16% y-o-y), held back by a low tax base in Q4 FY25. For FY26, revenue was INR 27.1 billion, EBITDA INR 6.10 billion (+26.3%) and PAT INR 4.55 billion (+19.1%). Management said inventory and data costs are rising as a deliberate investment in premium, verticalized inventory, and a roughly one-year investment phase is expected before margins improve. The board approved a preferential warrant issue to Affle Holdings (~INR 11 billion, 25% upfront) to fund acquisitions expected to be concluded within the calendar year.

financial_highlights.change: +20.3% y-o-y; margin broadly in line with Q4 FY25
+16.0% y-o-y, +0.2% q-o-q; subdued by low Q4 FY25 tax rate

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 PBT from operations (ex other income)

segments.name: CPCU business (Q4 FY26)
segments.commentary: 120.3 million conversions at a CPCU rate of INR 60.0, generating CPCU revenue of INR 7.21 billion.

segments.name: India + emerging markets (Q4 FY26)

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR99 crores (up about 55%), H1 INR183 crores (up 48%). Portfolio at a record 18.9 GW vs 13.5 GW in March; Q2 gross margin about 23%, guided to around 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at up to 10%; management later said this is roughly 10% and excludes Reliance orders, after an analyst noted the earlier range was 10-15%.
Q3 FY27 expected to be clearly better than H1; Q4 expected to be the strongest quarter.
EPC gross margin guided at 8% to 10%, depending on turnkey vs balance-of-system mix; O&M gross margin around 20%.
Full-year operational EBITDA margin of at least 4% to 4.5% described as a minimum requirement; recurring overheads expected at around 4.5% of revenue in FY27.
O&M revenue expected to exceed INR400 crores in FY27; O&M portfolio expected to reach 22-25 GW by year-end.

Around INR156 crores expected under indemnity from promoters in the current year.

Tilaiya floating solar project (Jharkhand, NTPC-DVC JV) nearing completion; power evacuation awaits state transmission line.

Reliance Kutch integrated renewable hub: site readiness underway, work expected post-monsoon; management said orders expected this quarter but would not give a size or date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for overheads and the Reliance order timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Recurring overheads are flat at about INR79-84 crores a quarter, about 5.5% of revenue now and expected near 4.5% for FY27; Reliance-related overhead increase is expected to be minimal as site costs sit in project budgets. Management gave no firm date for Reliance orders beyond 'some good news soon'.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company still expect 10% growth and EBITDA margin of 4-4.5%, and what are O&M targets?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the range was 10-15%, it now expects around 10% (not 0-1%), excluding Reliance, with possible support from international projects.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise despite lower execution?

qa_highlights.question: Banking limits, BGs and credit rating?

qa_highlights.question: O&M business model, margins and international expansion?

542772|2026-03.headline: 360 ONE WAM FY26 PAT rose 20.7% to Rs 1,225 crore, with ARR revenue at Rs 2,289 crore (up 34.5%) and total ARR AUM up 26% to Rs 3.12 lakh crore.
542772|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's highest full-year PAT at Rs 1,225 crore, up 20.7%, and total revenue rose 18.6% to Rs 3,144 crore. ARR revenue reached 75% of revenue from operations, with organic ARR net flows up 36% to Rs 35,199 crore. Transaction and broking revenue rose 4.4% for the year but jumped 53.7% in Q4 to Rs 230 crore, helped by full-quarter consolidation of 360 ONE Capital (ex-B&K Securities). Management reset its transaction revenue run-rate guidance upward to Rs 170-180 crore per quarter, and guided to 15-25% profit growth on Wealth for the coming years.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 35,199 crore (Wealth Rs 25,900 crore; AM Rs 9,299 crore)

financial_highlights.change: up 34.5% YoY; 75% of revenue from operations

financial_highlights.metric: Transaction and broking revenue Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: Q3 was 49.5% on cost to total operating income basis

segments.name: Wealth (UHNI)
segments.commentary: UHNI cost-to-income stable at 44-45%; Wealth organic net flows Rs 25,900 crore in FY26. Management targets 12-15% of opening AUM as annual net flows and 15-25% Wealth profit growth.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AM ARR AUM about Rs 95,000 crore; FY26 organic net flows Rs 9,299 crore. Q4 gross flows about Rs 5,200 crore, but net flows were about Rs 2,300-2,400 crore after about Rs 2,500-2,600 crore of maturities and distributions. Discretionary PMS flows have been soft.

segments.name: 360 ONE Capital (ex-B&K Securities)
segments.commentary: Full-quarter consolidation lifted Q4 TBR. B&K top line was about Rs 220-250 crore in the prior year, rising about 3-4% in the latest period, with PBT of about Rs 105-110 crore before acquisition costs. Investment banking build-out expected to contribute in 12-18 months.

segments.name: HNI reserve program
segments.commentary: About 60-65 RMs across 12 locations at closing, managing close to Rs 4,000 crore for 650-plus clients at about 90 bps yield. Management says revenue lags because the broker code change affects revenue only after 12 months.

segments.name: ET Money
segments.commentary: Undergoing strategic and business-model transformation; management expects breakeven in the near term without a specific timeline.

segments.name: Lending
segments.commentary: Largely Lombard / loan against shares, collateralised at 2x. Management reports no NPA and no loss since 2016; margin funding book under Rs 50-60 crore.

segments.name: Alternates carry
segments.commentary: Carryable AUM about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; carry accrual 5-7 bps in a bad year and 12-15 bps in a good year. Modelling assumption of about 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps total Alternates yield.

guidance_outlook: Wealth: target net flows of 12-15% of opening AUM annually; AUM growth of 20-25%; RM count growth of 25-30% a year over the next 3-4 years; Wealth profit growth 15-25%. Management said it may add 25-35 RMs this year.
Cost-to-income: long-term target of 46-48% on the overall business ex-new businesses, and 45-47% over 2-3 years; UHNI/AM core stays at 44-45%.

Transaction and broking revenue: run-rate now seen at Rs 170-180 crore per quarter (earlier Rs 125-130 crore); aspiration north of Rs 200 crore. Management said the Rs 175-200 crore range is not cast in stone and later suggested Rs 160-180 crore.
Equity and equity-related income (ex-banking) expected to nearly double over 3-4 years; equity research revenue on Wealth side of Rs 85-90 crore a year could double or triple in 3-5 years.
Banking: 12 senior investment professionals to hire, about 4 in place; management expects to be more competitive over the next 3-4 months.
Tangible ROE expected to improve as Lending and Alternates capital turns into earnings.
Management expects 2-4% attrition a year and aims to double market share over 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: Senior relationship managers: about 180-190 currently; target 330-340 (team leaders from about 70-75 to 120-130; partners from 110-120 to about 240).
UHNI RM count about 63-64 at closing (about 35-40 on an average basis during FY26), with plans to go to 25-35 extra RMs in FY27.
Wealth market share estimated at 8-10%, with about 4,500 families above Rs 10 crore; target 8,000-10,000 families.
Employee base about 1,800.
Alternates: 15-20 investment professionals per strategy; Lending with a dedicated team since 2016.
demand_pricing: Organic ARR net flows FY26 Rs 35,199 crore, of which Q4 net flows were about Rs 9,000-10,000 crore: advisory about Rs 4,500-5,000 crore, AM about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore, distribution and lending about Rs 2,000-2,500 crore.

Q4 AM gross flows about Rs 5,200 crore (FY26 about Rs 19,000 crore). Net flows reduced by a large credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE fund distribution.

Discretionary PMS flows were softer than desired; the strategy is being pivoted and relaunched around early June 2026. Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base. Negative distribution net flows of about Rs 212 crore were attributed mainly to corporate treasuries.
Management described 90% of cash segment share in broking, and over 500 mid- and small-cap companies under coverage.

Client base shift: family offices of about 400-500 clients (versus 40-50 five years ago); professionals now 15-20% of clients (from 5-10%); average ticket size rising due to a portfolio-based approach.

UBS collaboration: cross-referrals in NRI, resident and global mandates showing early traction. Regulatory approvals in GIFT City and on the UBS platform slowed progress; expected over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 transaction revenue (UHNI TBR) so strong, and will the Rs 125-130 crore per quarter benchmark be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TBR now looks closer to Rs 175-180 crore per quarter, helped by 360 ONE Capital and diversified asset-class mix (fixed income, REITs/InvITs, high-yield fixed income), and is more comfortable with Rs 170-180 crore than the earlier Rs 130-140 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2 to 3 year yield (ex-carry) decline, and what is the carry model?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield ex-carry seen as broadly stable. Carry is accrued at about 10-14 bps a year on carryable AUM of about Rs 30,000-35,000 crore; modelling assumption is 10 bps carry, so about 95-100 bps Alternates yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guided 20-25% AUM growth and RM addition consistent with 15-25% profit growth, given cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-income stays at 44-46% in the core UHNI and AM business, and operating leverage is high; it is willing to front-load RM hiring of 25-35 in FY27. Yield pressure and RM compensation are acknowledged but manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1 April 2026 mutual fund yield cut hit B&K transaction revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is about 2-3% on a base of about Rs 200-225 crore a quarter, which is not material, and is offset by synergies.

qa_highlights.question: Industry consolidation, competition, and attrition in UHNI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes the industry needs 3-4 or more large players but remains fairly consolidated for the next 3-4 years. It expects 2-4% attrition a year and sees 12-15% flows as doable.

qa_highlights.question: Quality of new clients, carry exits, and gross flows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said family office clients are growing and portfolio-based onboarding raises ticket sizes. Sanjay Wadhwa gave AM gross flows of about Rs 5,200 crore in Q4 and Rs 19,000 crore in FY26. Management said the fund-level carry list would be compiled later in a data book.

risks_watch: Execution risk as headcount scales: management calls execution the biggest risk, with about 1,800 employees and plans to add 25-35 UHNI RMs in FY27 while senior RM count moves from about 180-190 toward 330-340.

RM war for talent and compensation: management says it will hire between the 90th and 110th compensation percentile, and says cost-to-income could drift up during hiring; FY26 cost-to-income was 49.9%.
Wealth flow delivery: the 12-15% of opening AUM net flow target is described as a tall order, and management flagged that it gets harder as size increases.
Discretionary PMS outflows and pricing: DPMS flows are soft, the strategy is being pivoted with relaunch around early June 2026, and Q4 DPMS retention was inflated by profit share on a small base.

Alternates and carry: AM Q4 net flows were hit by a credit fund maturity (Rs 1,500-1,700 crore), a real estate fund maturity (about Rs 850 crore) and a 2021-vintage PE distribution; carry accrual depends on hurdle performance and market variation.

B&K/360 ONE Capital: the MF yield cut from 1 April 2026 (about 2-3% impact on Rs 200-225 crore quarterly base), TBR sustainability, and banking hiring (12 professionals, about 4 in place) with IB contribution expected in 12-18 months.
UBS collaboration and GIFT City regulatory approvals slowed progress; management expects movement over the next quarter.

We're investing heavily into middle management leadership depth.
So, yields ex of carry, actually, I'm not too worried about.
That's really where it is. So honestly, I agree with you on all the three points.

542772|2026-06.headline: 360 ONE Q1 FY27: total revenue up 20% to Rs 870 crore, PAT up 14.8% to Rs 330 crore, cost-to-income 51.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retention decline and how should it be viewed?

qa_highlights.question: Unit economics of UBS flows and effect on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said UBS flows are accretive without disproportionate cost; exact retention and unit economics to be seen over the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the TBR and transaction pipeline include large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Lumpy transactions are declining as co-investment vehicles convert deals into ARR. Listed equity brokerage of about Rs 75 crore a quarter is seen as the stable base; TBR target Rs 125-160 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 12-13 crore exceptional cost and the new ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 12-13 crore is ESOP cost linked to the B&K acquisition. The new 12 lakh SAR grant adds about Rs 60 crore over four years from next quarter.

risks_watch: Institutional mandate redemptions and weak FII and global allocation to listed equity could keep AM net flows volatile.
Retention pressure from listed AM (8-9% of revenue) and mix shift towards advisory.
Cost-to-income depends on ET Money break-even by Q4 FY27 and HNI migration of about 4,000 clients; new ESOPs add cost from next quarter.
ECM build-out is at an early stage and ECM contributes under Rs 8 crore a quarter; management targets 15-20% of a Rs 750-1,000 crore TBR base in 2-3 years.
UBS collaboration economics not yet disclosed; first fund launches expected next quarter.

542772|2026-09.headline: 360 ONE WAM Q2 FY27: revenue ₹853 crores (+4.8% YoY), PAT ₹302 crores, ARR AUM ₹3.53 lakh crores (+19.7% YoY), ARR net flows ₹12,482 crores.
542772|2026-09.overview: Total AUM was about ₹9 lakh crores (+31% YoY) and ARR revenue grew 27.5% YoY to ₹706 crores, now 79% of operating revenue. Headline revenue growth was held back by a negative ₹44 crore other income from mark-to-market on treasury investments, mainly NSE-linked fair value change of about ₹110-120 crores. Carry from third-party funds contributed about ₹60 crores, lifting ARR retention to 79 bps from 74 bps in Q1 (67 bps ex-carry). Cost-to-operating income improved to 51.5% from 54.3% in Q1, and tangible ROE was 16.9%.

financial_highlights.change: +15.5% YoY; employee costs ₹342 crores (+19.9%) incl. ~₹9 crores one-time restructuring

segments.name: Wealth
segments.commentary: ARR AUM ₹2,52,627 crores (+24.3% YoY); net flows ₹10,990 crores; ARR revenue ₹503 crores (+40.5% YoY); retention 79 bps (71 bps in Q1); operating PBT ₹326 crores (+30.2% YoY).

segments.name: Asset management
segments.commentary: ARR AUM a little over ₹1 lakh crores (+9.4% YoY); net flows ₹1,492 crores after large SMA redemptions in Q1; ARR revenue ₹203 crores at 79 bps; operating PBT ₹108 crores.

segments.name: Alternates (AIF)
segments.commentary: AIF AUM ₹58,139 crores (+27.9% YoY). Q2 AIF distributions about ₹2,500 crores vs net inflows about ₹2,500 crores, implying gross inflows of ₹4,800-4,900 crores.

segments.name: HNI business
segments.commentary: Manages over ₹8,000 crores for over 1,500 clients with about 60 RMs; ~2,000 relationships moved from UHNI, taking HNI AUM to ~₹8,800 crores; expects break-even on direct costs soon.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-operating income: guided 100-150 bps YoY improvement; management says on course, with a path toward 46-47% from 48% over 12-18 months.

UBS collaboration: internal target of about $600-650 million of flows exchanged in FY27; about $300-325 million moved in last three months; expects $600-700 million over the year. Expected retention on cross-flows 40-50 bps.
Tangible ROE: target around 20% over 3-3.5 years by doubling profits, with no equity raise needed; possible push toward 25% later. UBS warrant conversion (~₹1,600 crores) expected around February.
Capital markets: full-stack platform ready by end-March/early April 2027; banking and ECM mandates expected to flow from Q1 FY28; 8-10 issues appointed so far.
Equity brokerage from HNI/UHNI clients rose from ₹4.5-5 crores to ₹8-9 crores a month; potential ₹15-20 crores a month.
Fund P1A redemption of about ₹3,000-3,500 crores expected over the next 6-18 months.
capex_capacity: Tangible net worth about ₹7,400 crores, plus ~₹1,600 crores from UBS; management sees ~₹10,000-12,000 crores over the period with PAT of ~₹1,000-1,200 crores per year post dividend.
COMPASS proprietary AI layer is live across wealth, asset management and enterprise functions; runs inside the 360 ONE environment with no client data used to train external models.
ET Money ARR AUM about ₹3,300-3,400 crores including the distribution segment (over ₹700 crores ARR AUM in the last nine months).
demand_pricing: Q2 flows were supported by a strong IPO season (about 60 IPOs in the quarter) and monetization events; NSE listing was a major event. Wealth flows split about 50% from wallet share and 50% from new mandates, versus the usual 65-70% from new mandates.
New clients were about one-third of flows, existing clients two-thirds (management's broad split). Client attrition below 0.5% and AUM attrition below 0.25%.
Advisory retention on core portfolios 35-40 bps; large mandates around 20-25 bps; overall relationship retention 65-73 bps.
Management sees TBR as ~₹200-225 crores a quarter on ~₹1,000 crores revenue, growing late single to early double digits; mostly brokerage across six or seven asset classes.
On competition, management sees no dramatic margin compression; differentiation expected from people, product and platform together.
Mutual fund business: management plans measured growth, with possible sales-team build-out given SIF launch and 4-5 years of performance.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the mark-to-market change so large and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to secondaries market pricing; NSE-related fair value change of about ₹110-120 crores, largely held through funds. Prior quarter had a positive move.

qa_highlights.question: How do UBS flows progress and when do they come through?
qa_highlights.answer: About $300-325 million of flows moved in the last three months, with a target of $600-700 million for the year; funds recently empanelled and about $15 million came from UBS to 360 ONE initially.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company on track for the 48% cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO says on course for 100-150 bps YoY improvement; management targets a move from 48% toward 46-47% over 12-18 months, with productivity gains mainly in employee costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the role of new leadership hire Ashish Agarwal and the cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Senior leadership role spearheading the business with Karan Bhagat; first 6-8 months focused on integration. Three hires so far; cost-to-income could rise 100-200 bps during a big build, but expected to stay within that band.

qa_highlights.question: Why was AMC flow weaker, and what about carry reversals?
qa_highlights.answer: One institutional redemption split between Q1 and Q2; two institutional mandates won late in the quarter. Carry reversal on previously accrued NSE-linked carry was more than offset by new carry from NSE listing bringing funds into carry.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TBR outlook and how big are broking synergies from B&K?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says TBR is now mainly brokerage and was soft; expects ~₹800-1,000 crores TBR at ₹5,000-5,500 crores revenue. Equity brokerage from HNI/UHNI rose from ₹4.5-5 crores to ₹8-9 crores a month.

qa_highlights.question: How should AMC gross outflows be thought of from carry-linked funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Fund P1A (about ₹1,000 crores invested, now ₹3,000-3,500 crores value, NSE and CIBIL assets) to return money over 6-18 months; launches to be planned around that redemption.

qa_highlights.question: How does the ROE path to 20-25% look?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of about 20% tangible ROE over 3-3.5 years by doubling profits; 18-20% blended ROE considered comfortable given NBFC lending and 3-4% sponsor capital on alternates.

risks_watch: Mark-to-market volatility on treasury and NSE-linked fair value; other income was negative ₹44 crores this quarter.
Carry lumpiness and reversals; ~₹60 crores of carry this quarter; future carry sensitive to exits from funds.
AMC outflows from P1A redemption of ₹3,000-3,500 crores over 6-18 months; institutional mandate flow recovery to be confirmed.
UBS flow conversion versus the $600-700 million target and the warrant conversion timing (~February).
Competitive intensity from PE-backed digital players in UHNI, HNI and affluent segments; management says margins should hold.
Cost-to-income path toward 46-47% while adding senior hires; possible temporary rise of 100-200 bps during builds.
542772|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on wealth flows, platform breadth and UBS progress, but cautious on near-term AMC flows and TBR, which management called soft and structurally changing. Management was specific about targets and open about the carry and mark-to-market effects.

We do not judge COMPASS on usage, but on definite outcomes, which is efficiency, commercial impact, quality, and control.
If we can double our profits over the next 3.5 years and, honestly, don't see any need to raise capital. We can ensure that we hit the 20% number.

542773|2026-03.headline: FY26 operational revenue flat at INR2,439 crores as retail fell 9%, while Q4 operational revenue rose 20% YoY to INR644 crores.
542773|2026-03.overview: FY26 operational revenue was flat YoY at INR2,439 crores, with retail equity revenue down 9% to INR1,121 crores on SEBI regulatory changes that took full-year effect. Institutional and IB revenue rose 11% to INR712 crores and financial product distribution rose 16% to about INR590 crores. Q4 operational revenue grew 20% YoY to INR644 crores and 10% QoQ, but operational PBT fell 22% for the full year on higher employee costs. Management flagged market volatility from geopolitical events, record FPI outflows in March, and an income tax search with about INR56 crores of combined notices under appeal.

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR712 crores, up 11%; Q4 about INR162 crores, up from INR97 crores YoY and flat QoQ. Management split the current-period figure roughly as INR450 crores broking and INR250 crores banking.

segments.name: Financial product distribution (FPD)
segments.commentary: FY26 income close to INR600 crores (about INR590 crores), up 16%; Q4 INR182 crores, down 4% YoY on a high prior-year base but up 36% QoQ, driven by insurance and NCD/fixed income placements. FPD AUM about INR52,000 crores.

segments.name: Wealth / HNI channel
segments.commentary: New HNI channel AUM about INR12,000 crores with a product mix similar to the overall book. Around 50 wealth RMs and about 300 affluent/PCG broking RMs.

segments.name: Asset management and manufacturing
segments.commentary: Company has started in-house manufacturing on PMS and AIF platforms (early stage, late stage and credit). Capital Credit Opportunities fund closed, raising about INR500 crores.

guidance_outlook: No explicit FY27 AUM or revenue guidance; management said it has no specific AUM target in mind but must increase assets.
Management expects capital to support about 20% growth over the next couple of years without new capital, per Q&A.
Short-term impact expected from RBI F&O-related margin rules effective 1 July, with marginal direct impact because the company does no prop trading.
Management views the reset of domestic mutual fund yields from 1 April as having a marginal impact on realisations.
Management expects to add wealth RMs in FY27 but gave no number.
capex_capacity: Investments in branches and technology drove depreciation up 20% in FY26 and 6% YoY in Q4 (new branch commissioned).
Finance cost rise tied to working capital needs from MTF book growth.
Net worth grew from about INR1,000 crores to INR3,000-plus crores over four years, entirely from accruals, per management.
Capital deployed mainly in broking, MTF and exchange margins; in-house PMS and AIF manufacturing started.
demand_pricing: Management attributed the sequential MTF book decline to market volatility in the last quarter.

Within total FY26 income of about INR419-420 crores in interest-related income, management said roughly 50% related to MTF and 50% to deposits; MTF interest was about INR160-170 crores, interest expense about INR180 crores.
Clients will bear higher F&O trading costs from the new margin rules.
Q4 FPD jump attributed to insurance and NCD/fixed income placements.
Retail regulatory changes from SEBI, effective in the first quarter of the prior calendar year, caused the full-year retail decline.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FPD AUM growth, and how many RMs were added and planned for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FPD AUM rose from about INR31,000 crores to INR52,000 crores, with growth across MF (INR14,000 to about INR21,000 crores), PMS, AIF and fixed income. About 50 wealth RMs and 300 affluent/PCG RMs; management aims to grow wealth RMs but gave no number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the MTF book decline sequentially, and what is the Q4 institutional broking/IB split?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline attributed to market volatility in the last quarter. Institutional revenue roughly INR700 crores split about INR450 crores broking and INR250 crores banking, rough figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is a fund raise planned, and what would the funds be used for?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share details, saying the Board evaluates acquisitions and projects continuously and will disclose when definitive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI rules from 1 July and of MF yield reset from 1 April?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term impact on working capital and margins; marginal impact on the company as it does no prop trading. Yield reset impact seen as marginal since effective yield was already near the regulator's suggested range.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the HNI channel and what is its product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR12,000 crores of AUM through the new HNI channel, with a product mix similar to the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NII/net interest margin, and how is MTF interest split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated net interest spread at about 4% and said MTF and deposit interest split roughly 50-50. Attribution is hard, so the answer was incomplete; the analyst was invited to a follow-up meeting.

qa_highlights.question: Any color on Fairfax stake increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment and said it would disclose once there is something definitive.

qa_highlights.question: Can net worth of about INR3,000 crores support growth, and are new businesses planned such as an AMC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has enough capital for about 20% growth. Core businesses are IB, insurance, equities and wealth management; in-house PMS and AIF manufacturing has started, and new opportunities will be evaluated.

risks_watch: Sustained market volatility and record FPI outflows in March; the trend was said to continue.
Margin and working capital rules from 1 July could hit F&O volumes and client activity.
Employee cost growth (including variable pay) is outpacing revenue, pressuring operational PBT.

Fairfax possibly raising its stake by 10%; management declined to comment.

542773|2026-06.headline: IIFL Capital Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR631 crore; distribution income fell 31% QoQ while institutional/IB rose 27% to INR207 crore.
542773|2026-06.overview: Consolidated operational revenue was INR631 crore, flat QoQ and YoY. Retail broking revenue was flat QoQ at INR297 crore, while institutional broking and IB income rose 27% QoQ to INR207 crore. Financial product distribution fell about 31% QoQ to INR125 crore, which management attributed to the seasonal Q4 insurance peak and lumpy transactional income booked in Q4. Operational PBT was INR149 crore, up 4% QoQ but down about 9% YoY; other income jumped to about INR90 crore on mark-to-market gains on BSE shares.

segments.name: Institutional broking and investment banking
segments.commentary: Combined revenue INR207 crore, up 27% QoQ. Institutional equities roughly INR200 crore combined with IB; split roughly 50:50 or 60:40 by management.

segments.name: Financial product distribution
segments.commentary: Income INR125 crore, down about 31% QoQ and 14% YoY, due to absence of Q4 insurance peak and lower lumpy transactional income. guidance_outlook: Management expects AUM growth to catch up next quarter after a slower Q1 in net collections of about INR3,675 crore.

Margins were pressured by a one-time HR/gratuity charge of about INR20 crore, proof-of-concept costs on six trains, a West Asia-driven resin cost spike in Rail Neer, and lower non-convenience fee income in internet ticketing. segments.name: Rail Neer

segments.name: Tourism
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168 crore (+13.5%); EBITDA margin improved to 11.31% from 8.78% on better product mix and cost realisation, despite geopolitical disruption. Non-fare revenue from Tejas naming/wrap rights noted as a new lever.

On a Vande Bharat basis, the licence fee plus GST earns about INR105 per unit against INR222 paid to licensees, with about INR11 of non-claimable GST. Management said the 10-12% traditional catering margin range is the target.

542857|2026-06.headline: Greenpanel Q1 FY27 combined revenue rose 8.5% to INR350 crore and EBITDA turned positive at INR32.5 crore, but exports fell to zero and OEM volumes degrew 14%.

Price hikes of around 15% taken in April were largely rolled back by peers through May to July, so realisations are now close to pre-hike levels. Exports fell to zero and OEM sales degrew 14%, while domestic MDF volumes grew 12% YoY and retail MDF grew about 20%. Management declined to give margin or utilisation guidance, citing daily chemical cost and discount volatility.

542867|2026-03.headline: CSB Bank FY26 net profit rose 7% to Rs.633 crore; Q4 profit Rs.202 crore (+32% QoQ) with GNPA at a low 1.66%.

Asset quality improved to GNPA 1.66% and NNPA 0.40%, helped by lower slippages and higher recoveries. Management guided retail asset growth only from FY28, CTI of 60-65% through FY27, and RoA/RoE of about 1.5%/15% next year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management cited new liability products (Smart Save, Freedom current accounts), a TASC vertical, school fee financing and LAS against mutual funds, plus transaction banking going live in 3-4 months.

rows.label: Wholesale relationship team expansion and corporate book growth
rows.why: Relationship team expanded from low double digits to 80-plus, but corporate growth is only described as progressing as planned with no figure given.

rows.label: Gold share of book toward 30% by 2030

rows.label: ECL transition on April 1, 2027

542867|2026-06.headline: CSB Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 27% YoY to Rs.150 Crores, with NIM at 3.66% and ROA at 1.09%, but other income fell 7%.
542867|2026-06.overview: CSB Bank reported Q1 FY27 net profit of Rs.150 Crores (+27% YoY) and operating profit of Rs.251 Crores (+14% YoY), with NII up 26% to Rs.479 Crores. Deposits grew 26% and advances 24% YoY, both ahead of industry, and CD ratio moved to just under 90%. Other income fell 7% YoY on lower treasury gains (Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores) and weaker insurance and gold-linked processing fees. Management called Q1 the worst-case margin quarter and reiterated FY27 NIM of around 3.75% and ROA of 1.3%-1.5%.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.12 Crores treasury profit plus Rs.3 Crores trading profit (total other income down 7%)
Growth 24% YoY vs industry 18.6%; yield on advances 10.65%

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: About 54% of the loan book; yield 11.85% vs 12% QoQ. Management expects the gold mix to stay near 50% in FY27 and fall toward 30% by FY2030. Gold disbursements fell QoQ on regulatory implementation and reduced top-ups; the book was about Rs.21,000 Crores last quarter.

segments.name: Wholesale (WSB)
segments.commentary: About 26% of the book; growing 35%-40% per management. Target is about 32% of the book by FY2030. FIPS book fell to about one-third of WSB from about 70%.

segments.name: SME / BLG
segments.commentary: Yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ. Slippages in the quarter; management is deliberately cautious and has raised credit appraisal bars for FY27.

segments.name: Retail (LAS / repledger)
segments.commentary: Repledger LAS book fell from over Rs.2,100 Crores to about Rs.60 Crores and will run off by next quarter, per RBI discontinuation from 1 April 2026. Unsecured retail is only about 2% of the book; focus deferred to FY2028.

segments.name: Treasury and fee income
segments.commentary: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, and insurance fees fell after tighter mis-selling controls. Management targets full-year fee income at 16%-17% of total income, with Q1 other income about 15% of income.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 NIM guidance of around 3.75%; management said it sees no risk to this guidance.
Full-year FY27 ROA guidance of 1.3%-1.5%; management said it would not go below 1.3% this year and internal target is 1.5%.
ROE: started FY27 near 12%; aims to end FY27 above the FY26 exit of 14.14% and try to touch 15%.
Wholesale to grow 35%-40% and gold 30%-35% in FY27; gold mix expected near 50% this year.
CASA to grow in line with deposits from FY2028; CASA to outgrow term deposits from FY2029. FY27 CASA ratio expected to hold at about 19.4% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Fee income guidance of 16%-17% of total income for the full year, with insurance and gold disbursements expected to pick up from Q2.
Unsecured retail push deferred to FY2028; ECLGS disbursement so far about Rs.60 Crores.
capex_capacity: Network of 868 branches and 835 ATMs as on 30 June 2026.

New retail liability acquisition channel rolling out; retail deposit products launched last year, with sales team being built.
Technology was delayed by about two and a half years, per management, due to a decision delay rather than execution.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth 26% YoY vs industry 13.4%; bulk deposits about 52% of term deposits and about 40% of total deposits; retail about 48% of deposits.
Cost of funds around 6.5%; higher cost driven by bulk deposits, FCY borrowings and CDs, which management expects to ease as liquidity improves.
Q1 NIM hit by flow-through of end-March deposit costs, and by slippages and reduced recoveries; management says Q1 NIM is the worst case for the year.
Gold LTV around 75% vs peers below 65%, driven by agri gold (LTV up to 85%); non-agri LTV about 50%-55%. Board plans to gradually cut agri gold.
Deposit rates showing marginal softening; SME yields expected to improve next quarter as slippages are upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Gold share at 54%, bulk deposits at 52% of term deposits; is the bulk mix the main NIM drag and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the bulk mix (about 52% of term deposits) raises cost of funds (about 6.5%). Retail franchise build starts with CASA from FY2028; management expects no quick reduction in bulk share in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Can a wholesale book funded by wholesale money hold margins, and how volatile are slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM and ROA guidance holds for the year; wholesale is being built as a franchise with ROA and RAROC targets. Q1 slippage about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores), mainly in BLG/SME, which management expects to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall 7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Treasury profit was Rs.12 Crores vs Rs.53 Crores a year ago, insurance fees were cut after mis-selling controls, and gold/retail processing fees fell with lower disbursements. Management expects recovery from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 ROA guidance being revised from around 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will not go below 1.3% for FY27, with an internal 1.5% target; the 1.3% comment answered a different question on the year-end run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of IDBI Bank stake sale by promoter Fairfax?
qa_highlights.answer: CSB has had no discussions on this. Fairfax told management to continue business as usual; the bank is run by its own management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gold disbursements fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regulatory implementation (end-use monitoring), fewer top-ups as gold prices stopped rising, and the repledger LAS run-off. Disbursements are expected to pick up as gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS disbursement and what is the growth guidance for corporate and gold?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS disbursements about Rs.60 Crores so far. Management guided wholesale at 35%-40% growth and gold at 30%-35% for FY27.

risks_watch: Asset quality volatility: slippages of about Rs.98 Crores in Q1 vs Rs.60 Crores in Q4, concentrated in BLG/SME; upgrade assumption for Q2/Q3 is key.
Margin pressure from bulk and CD funding (cost of funds about 6.5%); the NIM path depends on deposit repricing and CD rates easing.
Other income recovery depends on treasury gains (AFS book) and insurance and gold fee pick-up from Q2.
Gold regulation: end-use monitoring and the gold mix glide path from 54% toward 30% by FY2030.
Execution of the CASA/retail franchise, with CASA ratio expected to hold at 19.41% only if deposits grow about 25%.
Management said Q1 ROA of 1.09% is below the FY27 guidance of 1.3%-1.5%, so the run-rate must improve materially in later quarters.
542867|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the year-on-year numbers and guidance, but defensive on the quarter-on-quarter dip in NIM, ROA and other income, which it attributes to transient factors. Management was also candid about the delayed technology decision and avoided commenting on the IDBI Bank stake sale beyond saying it was not involved.
key_quotes: We will only improve from here.
In 2027 itself we will touch 1.3%.
I do not see liquidity as a risk for us in the near term.

Except for the technology which got delayed by around two-and-a-half years which was a decision point and not an execution point - almost everything else we achieved the way we had given guidance to the markets.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 NIM at about 3.75% and ROA at 1.3-1.5%, and Q1 ROA of 1.09% is well below the 1.3% floor, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.why: Q1 slippages of about Rs.98 Crores (Q4 about Rs.60 Crores) are expected to be largely upgraded in Q2/Q3, and SME yield fell to 9.25% from 9.81% QoQ, so NIM and asset quality recovery depends on this.

rows.label: Fee income recovery to 16-17% of total income
rows.why: Q1 other income was about 15% of income and treasury profit fell to Rs.12 Crores from Rs.53 Crores YoY; management expects insurance and gold fees to pick up from Q2.

rows.label: Repledger LAS run-off complete

542867|2026-09.headline: CSB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 22% QoQ to Rs.183 Cr, with NIM up to 3.81% and ROA to 1.29%.
542867|2026-09.overview: CSB Bank reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs.183 Cr, up 22% QoQ and 14% YoY, with net interest income of Rs.510 Cr (up 7% QoQ, 20% YoY). NIM widened to 3.81% from 3.66% in Q1, driven by a higher yield on advances (10.92%) and stable cost of funds. Fee income rebounded 20% QoQ, though overall fee income was down about 22% YoY due to market-linked non-core lines. Asset quality improved on GNPA (1.58%) and NNPA (0.33%), with credit cost at 24 bps, though elevated write-offs of fully provided card and unsecured book were flagged. Management said it is entering a "scale phase" with retail liability build-out, SME growth restarting, and guidance of ROA 1.5% to 1.8% next year.

financial_highlights.change: +20% QoQ; ex-treasury +27% QoQ; fee income -22% YoY
vs 3.66% in Q1 FY27 and 3.81% in Q2 FY26
Yield on advances 10.92% vs 10.65% in Q1
PCR 87.65% (79.19% without PWO); credit cost 24 bps

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book grew 36% YoY, but tonnage fell about 6% YoY and disbursements slowed; management targets gold at about 50% of loan mix by year-end (53% last year, 54% last quarter), with a 32% glide path by 2030. Gold yields rose about 50 bps QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate / wholesale
segments.commentary: Corporate segment grew 44% YoY; wholesale split roughly equally across corporate banking, mid-market and FIs, with corporate and mid-market growing faster.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: SME growth remained flattish after exits and customer losses on pricing; management expects SME growth to resume from this quarter after portfolio issues were corrected.

segments.name: Retail (ex-gold)
segments.commentary: Retail growth was muted; the bank degrew loan against security (repledge gold loans, now almost zero) and is keeping unsecured cards, agri and MFI cautious, with unsecured retail to restart around FY2028.

segments.name: Fee income
segments.commentary: Core fee grew about 27% YoY and is just short of 15% of total income; overall fee is just short of 17% of total income (vs 23% last year, which included one-offs). Non-core lines (PSLC, treasury) declined.

guidance_outlook: ROA this year expected between 1.30% and 1.5%; next year (FY28) targeted at 1.5% to 1.8%, closer to 1.5% initially.
NIM guided at around 3.75% to 3.8% this year; around 3.75% next year.
Cost of funds to be brought down from 6.55% to about 6% next financial year.
Fee to total income assumed at 17% to 18%; IRDAI corporate agency draft may cut this by 0.5% to 1%.
Balance sheet growth guided at 30% to 50% faster than the system; system growth was faster this quarter due to FCNR inflows.
CASA to grow faster than term deposits from FY2028, after being slower this year.
Gold loans to fall to about 50% of mix by year-end; SBS 2030 targets continue.
capex_capacity: Network of 872 branches and 844 ATMs as at September 2026.
Core system upgrade and DC-DR switch completed; OFSAA implementation under way.
Technology investments span transaction banking (supply chain, CMS, trade), OBDX, corporate net banking and corporate LOS.
Management plans to launch 3-4 retail liability products every quarter, with current account acquisition the current focus.
Opex up about 11% QoQ and about 3% YoY; other opex up 18% QoQ mainly on technology, plus distribution and infrastructure; staff cost up about 17% YoY.
demand_pricing: Gold disbursements fell as rebooking is no longer shown as new disbursement and gold prices dipped; management says the regulator's LTV cut from 90% to 75% was managed.
Gold loan LTV about 75% vs 60-65% at peers, attributed to a larger agri portfolio where higher LTV is allowed; about 28% of gold book is above Rs.20 lakh ticket size.
Gold yields raised by about 50 bps QoQ, leveraging distribution and competitor pricing.
Lost some SME customers on pricing; exited a list of customers after quality review.
Deposit mix about 48% retail and 52% wholesale; FCY, CDs and borrowings remain significant funding sources.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other opex rise 18% QoQ and is it linked to higher other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total opex rose about 11% QoQ and 3% YoY; the rise was mainly technology, plus distribution expansion and infrastructure spends. Staff cost was up about 17% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in yield on advances and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Better asset quality, careful yield management in wholesale and SME, and a gold yield increase of about 50 bps QoQ, helped by distribution reach and competitor pricing. Cost of funds was flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why were write-offs high while credit cost was low?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wrote off a fully provided vintage of credit card and unsecured loans with low recovery prospects and no PSL benefit; it said this had no impact on credit cost, which was 24 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI corporate agency consultation paper on fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, so guidance may drop from 18% to 17% short term, with the bank aiming to recover through core fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the balance sheet growth outlook and retail deposit traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated growth 30% to 50% faster than system; retail current account acquisition has started, and liability franchise takes two to three years to build. Asset growth is not the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is Fairfax or IDBI relevant to CSB, and is there a Fairfax deposit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fairfax has no deposits with the bank and the board has not discussed the Fairfax/IDBI matter; the transaction is still incomplete.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROA and NIM outlooks for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of 1.30-1.5% this year, 1.5-1.8% next year; NIM around 3.75-3.8%, with cost of funds targeted at about 6% next year to offset mix shift.

risks_watch: Gold loan tonnage down about 6% YoY and gold disbursements slowing; gold book mix must fall to about 50%.
Regulatory fee risk from IRDAI corporate agency draft; fee-to-income could fall 0.5-1%.
Asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm; management points to a declining non-gold SMA book.
Cost of funds at 6.55% and reliance on FCY borrowings, CDs and bulk deposits; CASA ratio slipped to 18.96%.
Opex growth (other opex +18% QoQ) and cost-to-income at 64.8% against the fee and NIM outlook.
Interpretation risk on write-offs: elevated write-offs of fully provided book alongside PCR rising to 87.65%.
542867|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on earnings momentum, ROA and the scale phase, but guarded on the timing of retail growth, CASA recovery and the fee impact from the IRDAI draft. Management declined to elaborate on the other income breakup and deflected the Fairfax/IDBI question as not yet relevant.
key_quotes: Overall, we had a fairly good quarter.

We will start seeing the growth on the SME side from this quarter onwards because most of the portfolio-related issues we faced in SME book for the last one-and-a-half years have been by and large corrected now.
I would say that we would aim to bring down the cost of funds to somewhere around 6% next financial year, which will give us a 50-basis points lift.

rows.label: SME growth restarts after portfolio clean-up
rows.why: SME growth was flattish after exits and pricing-driven customer losses; management expects it to resume from this quarter, but the asset quality trend needs two to three more quarters to confirm.

rows.label: IRDAI corporate agency draft fee impact
rows.why: Management estimates a 0.5% to 1% drag on fee-to-income, which would move guidance from 18% to about 17%.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, ROA trajectory and the scale phase, but cautious on gold tonnage, retail growth timing, CASA recovery and the IRDAI fee draft; analysts pushed on write-offs, other opex and the Fairfax/IDBI matter, which management deflected.

542904|2026-03.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q4FY26: Q4 PAT annualised to ROA 2.1%, but FY27 guidance of ~1.6% ROA, ~25% advances growth and 1.4-1.5% credit cost.
542904|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 showed strong operating momentum: NII rose 26.4% YoY to INR1,092 crores, NIM improved to 8.5%, disbursements hit a record INR9,811 crores, and gross loan book reached INR40,655 crores (+26.6% YoY). Exit-quarter PAT was INR282 crores (ROA 2.1%, ROE 17.2%) versus FY26 PAT of INR693 crores (ROA 1.4%, ROE 10.9%). The RBI returned the bank's application for voluntary transition to a universal bank; management will reapply later with a more diversified portfolio. Management guided to a higher secured mix (about 56% by March 2027), a board-approved equity raise of up to INR2,000 crores in H2FY27, and FY27 ROA of around 1.6%, below the Q4 exit rate.

segments.name: Secured portfolio
segments.commentary: Reached INR20,079 crores (+43.5% YoY, +12.6% QoQ), now 49.4% of gross book. Housing +43.4% YoY and MSME +57.9% YoY; the housing vertical crossed INR10,000 crores.

segments.name: Micro banking
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR20,709 crores (+6.9%); Q4 disbursements a record INR5,245 crores (+11.9% QoQ). FY26 new customer additions 5.4 lakh. Management guides FY27 growth below 10%, a higher single digit.

segments.name: Newer lines (gold, vehicle, agri)
segments.commentary: Grew 292%, 102% and 127% YoY respectively; together about 6% of loan mix versus 3% in FY25. Gold yield is above 14%; micro mortgage yield is 19.7%.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Retail TD plus CASA INR31,955 crores (70% of deposits). CD ratio 89%, LCR 142%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 advances growth around 25%: secured about 40% and unsecured about 10%, per the Chief Credit Officer.
FY27 credit cost moderates to 1.4-1.5% of average GLB (exit quarter DuPont credit cost about 1.1%, per the call).
FY27 ROA around 1.6%, base case, with upside possible; NIM guided at around 8.5%, in line with the Q4 exit level.
Opex to ATA 20-30bps above FY26 in FY27 due to investment, then expected to decline; cost to income to stay at FY26 levels.
Secured share about 56% by March 2027. CASA ratio about 29-30% (Head of Retail Liabilities said around 30%).

Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, planned for H2FY27. About 20% branch addition in FY27 (about 140 branches on 776 base). Cost of deposits to benefit about 25-30bps from SA rate cuts; no TD repricing planned.
capex_capacity: Branch network 776 as of March 2026; FY27 plan to add about 20% (about 140 branches, confirmed by management as broadly yes).
Digital, AI and analytics investment on a cloud-led data platform; the spend is driving the opex increase.
Equity raise up to INR2,000 crores, to maintain buffer over the Board-mandated 20% CAR threshold and fund growth for about 3 years.
No inorganic acquisition of secured book is planned.
demand_pricing: Industry bank credit grew 16% to INR219 lakh crore and deposits 13.4% to INR268 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026.
Management cut SA rates in April; expects a 25-30bps reduction in SA cost of funds. SA exit cost of funds was 5.21% in March.
No plan to reprice retail or bulk TDs or MFI yields; management is watching competitors who have raised TD rates.
Gold ticket size rose about 60% YoY, with yields up about 30bps QoQ after lowering rates on small tickets.
Management said deposit growth will match credit growth; a slowdown in deposits in the July-August period was deliberate because of excess liquidity.
MFI slippages for Q4 around INR130 crores; Bucket-X collection efficiency 99.8% in March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why does ROA fall from about 2% to 1.6% if NIM, opex and credit cost are flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is conservative on opex and credit cost and covers possible stress in a couple of key products; no specific line item was identified. It will update if the number changes materially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the secured mix shift cut yields and margins, and how much cost-of-funds benefit is left?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30bps of deposit repricing benefit remains. Management cites 2-wheeler, gold (above 14%) and micro mortgage (19.7%) yields to offset lower housing and MSME yields. NIM guided at about 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when CAR is already strong?
qa_highlights.answer: The asset growth guidance is 25% a year against a Board threshold of 20%, and the bank needs growth capital for about 3 years. The raise is planned for H2FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow MFI faster, with a larger share of new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Most FY26 acquired customers are not yet eligible for repeat loans, so growth will be mostly repeat-driven. New-to-bank share is about 25%, possibly rising to 30%, but not 40-45%, which would be too risky.

qa_highlights.question: What is the secured mix target and reapplication timeline for universal bank status?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI gives no ratio. Management expects about 56% secured by March 2027, and the reapplication timeline will be set after a 2-3 year plan, not immediately.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a contingency provision buffer for ECL or universal bank readiness in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management has no plan for additional provisions in FY27 beyond the guidance.

risks_watch: ROA guidance of 1.6% sits well below the 2.1% exit rate; management gave no line-item bridge, and the opex investment and mix shift are the main drivers to track.
Secured yield dilution as the mix moves toward housing and MSME; monitor NIM against the 8.5% guide.
Deposit competition: peers have raised TD rates; the bank has no plan to match, so CASA and TD growth need watching.
Micro banking growth held below 10% as repeat-loan-driven; watch the 5.4 lakh new-customer run-rate and any guardrail changes.

West Asia conflict and oil price exposure: management says the book has no FX lending and no oil, gas, defence or aviation exposure, but is tightening 2-wheeler, used vehicle and MSME working capital monitoring.
Equity raise timing (H2FY27) and dilution; universal bank reapplication timeline still undefined.
542904|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating momentum and asset quality, but evasive on the bridge from the 2.1% exit ROA to the 1.6% FY27 guide, deferring to opex and credit cost conservatism. Cautious on the universal bank reapplication, which management said will not happen immediately.
key_quotes: Our financial outcome for Q4 reflects near-normal portfolio and operational performance.
The RBI does not share, direct, or guide a particular ratio.
We are being conservative on both our opex and our credit cost.
So we have broadly constructed our secured and unsecured ratio for this year.

542904|2026-06.headline: Ujjivan SFB Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR317 crore (ROA 2.2%, ROE 18.2%); FY27 ROA guidance raised to 1.8-2.0%.

segments.name: Affordable housing and micro mortgages

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,020 crore (+248.6% YoY); Q1 disbursements INR467 crore (+183.9% YoY). Sourced from 455 branches (106 added in the quarter); origination LTV 75%, book LTV about 56%.

segments.name: Vehicle loans
segments.commentary: Book INR1,036 crore (+85.1% YoY), GNPA 1.7%, served through 337 branches with a mid-premium and EV focus. New lines (gold, vehicle, agri) are 7% of the loan book and 9% of Q1 disbursements.

FY27 opex expected at about 6.4% of average assets, lower than earlier plan, as capacity spend (about INR250 crore) is deferred to later quarters.
FY27 planned asset growth of 25% reaffirmed.

Opex to decline year-on-year in FY28 as investment intensity eases.

qa_highlights.question: Can yields be sustained in affordable housing and non-MFI segments, and is 2% ROA possible on a steady-state basis?

qa_highlights.question: Will cost of funds rise further, and is any more deposit rate hike needed?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity-building spend and does the guidance embed NIM compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Bala Kamath said about INR250 crore planned, with little spent in Q1 and spend starting in June; the 1.8-2.0% ROA guidance includes it. NIM guidance given at the start of the year is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the credit cost guidance cut and are there early warning signs in MFI?

qa_highlights.question: What is the micro mortgage PAR and LGD outlook?

Management said June and July saw recovery in channel restocking, and it reiterated FY27 guidance of 12-15% volume growth and 11-13% EBITDA margin. Inventory days rose to 100, which management attributed to supply insecurity during the war and a volume shortfall, and it expects normalisation to 65-75 days by end-September quarter.

guidance_outlook: Cost-to-income expected in the 55-58% range for FY27, with no major step-up from corporate spends.
NIM expected to remain stable, at risk from any significant rise in cost of funds.
Credit cost expected to moderate further in FY27, dependent on geopolitical and macro developments.
No guidance on asset (receivables) growth; asset growth expected to follow card acquisition.
Medium-term ROA target of 4% to 4.5%, described as achievable.
No cost-of-funds guidance for FY27; around 70-75% of borrowings are floating (T-bill or repo linked) and reprice in 60-90 day buckets.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, utilisation data or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the call covered only card acquisition volumes (917,000 new accounts in Q4 vs 0.9-1.0 million quarterly target, expected to be in a similar range next quarter) and asset growth tied to acquisition, with no asset growth guidance given.
Digital onboarding via SBI Card Sprint is described as growing in share of new account acquisitions; no capacity or cost figures were disclosed for it.
Management said it is poised to harness AI and ML investments in FY27 for product development, service delivery and collections; no capex amount or timeline was given.
Collections infrastructure, digital and physical, was strengthened during the year; no capex or capacity quantification was provided.
demand_pricing: Industry credit card spends grew ~12% YoY to INR23.62 trillion in FY26 per RBI; cards-in-force above 118.6 million; SBI Card cards-in-force share 18.6%.
Management attributed muted industry card growth to issuers tightening underwriting after asset quality issues, with few new-to-credit customers being acquired.
Banca NTC/NTCC share estimated at 20-30% of banca-sourced customers; Q4 new-sourcing mix 70% salaried.
Rental spends are now a very small category after fee levy; UPI-on-credit growth 10% in Q4 vs Q3.
Management said FY26 corporate spends (with passback costs) raised both income and opex, thinning margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why is new account addition lower, and what is the cost-to-income outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 acquisition of 917,000 was on track with the 0.9-1.0 million target; cost-to-income guided 55-58% for FY27 as corporate-spend passback costs normalise, not employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revolver downside plan and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a revolver floor; first offset is instalment lending rather than cutting rewards. Cost of funds guidance deferred given RBI and geopolitical uncertainty; repricing to continue for about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the one-quarter INR100 crore management overlay increase run through P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR100 crore additional ECL provision is charged to P&L; without it profit would be INR100 crore higher. Overlay retained at INR220 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the dividend paid when profit growth was ~13%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capital adequacy (25.5%) is comfortable and the company is underleveraged, so INR2.50 per share was seen as a fair return to shareholders.

qa_highlights.question: Will receivables growth accelerate in FY27 or only FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No asset growth guidance was given; management reiterated that asset growth will follow card acquisition at 0.9-1.0 million per quarter.

risks_watch: Revolver ratio (22%) drifting lower; instalment book offset is not expected to fully compensate; NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise.
Receivables growth at ~2% YoY; no guidance given on asset growth.
Opex and cost-to-income: Q4 adjusted cost-to-income near 60% after one-offs; FY27 guidance 55-58%.
Geopolitical and macro uncertainty affecting credit cost moderation and the pace of ECL model refresh.
Q4 YoY instalment decline and loss of Apple offer; management called these transient, within 3-6 months.
Recovery pool (~INR190 crore) and write-offs trending lower; not disclosed in size.
543066|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability trends, but cautious and non-committal on growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 asset growth and cost of funds.
key_quotes: Overall, the business is profitable, but the margins are comparatively thinner, which basically boost both on the cost and the income side.
So we are building on card acquisition, and we expect that the asset growth will follow the card acquisition growth.
We are underleveraged actually, if you look at that.
we are aiming towards 4% to 4.5% of ROA in the medium term. And that is achievable and we are working towards it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Credit cost expected to moderate further (Q4 gross credit cost 7.7%, down 55 bps QoQ) and ROA target 4-4.5% medium term, but NIM guided stable and cost-to-income 55-58% (FY26 55.3%) leaves little room for expansion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Card acquisition of ~917,000 new accounts in Q4 with next quarter expected in a similar 0.9-1.0 million range, but receivables only ~2% YoY and no asset growth guidance given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plans, capacity or utilisation data discussed; only AI/ML investment mentioned with no amount or timeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Only stable NIM, moderating credit cost and cost-to-income held at 55-58%; no revenue or receivables growth guidance, and receivables grew only ~2% YoY to INR56,926 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revolver rate (22%) drifting lower and NIM at risk from cost-of-funds rise (Q4 cost of funds 6.4%, ~70-75% of borrowings floating), with FY27 cost-to-income guided at 55-58% versus FY26 55.3% and Q4 near 60% adjusted.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches discussed beyond instalment lending as an offset to revolver decline.

rows.label: Instalment lending as revolver offset
rows.why: Management leaning on instalment lending to offset revolver rate drift from 22-24%, though it is not expected to fully compensate and Q4 instalment saw a YoY decline.

rows.label: Underleveraged balance sheet with 25.5% CAR
rows.why: CAR 25.5% and management calls the company underleveraged, implying headroom for faster growth if acquisition converts into receivables, but no growth guidance was given.

rows.label: Corporate-spend passback costs normalise
rows.why: Management said cost-to-income guided at 55-58% as passback costs normalise after FY26 opex rose 22% YoY, with Q4 cost-to-income at 57.2%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GNPA 2.41%, credit cost 7.7%) and profitability, but cautious and non-committal on receivables growth, cost of funds and revolver mix, declining to quantify FY27 asset growth; analysts pressed on revolver downside and growth.
